Pointing to a specific geographical box, a specific altar, or a piece of matter and claiming that the physical Christ is located right there is precisely what Jesus warned His disciples to ignore. (2) The book of Hebrews demolishes the idea of a continually repeated physical presentation of Christ on an earthly altar. Scripture states that Jesus “after he had offered ONE SACRIFICE FOR SINS FOR EVER, sat down on the right hand of God” (Heb 10:12 KJV) - “sat down”, meaning it’s completed for ever. (3) Structurally, Jesus’ resurrected, glorified body is currently located in heaven. Peter explicitly preached that “heaven must receive [Him] until the times of restitution of all things” (Acts 3:21 KJV). Jesus does return PHYSICALLY in fragments across thousands of church altars daily. Spiritually, He dwells inside the hearts of believers as the Holy Spirit that He is: “But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that THE SPIRIT OF GOD dwell in you. Now if any man have not THE SPIRIT OF CHRIST, he is none of his” (Rom 8:9 KJV) - notice “Spirit of God” is used interchangeably with the “Spirit of Christ.” And recall there is only one Spirit (Eph 4:4). Another verse is: “After THE HOLY SPIRIT had prevented them from speaking..” & then clarifies whose Spirit: “THE SPIRIT OF JESUS would not permit them” (Acts 16:6-7 BSB) - the CT adds clarity to the TR in that the “Spirit of Jesus” is the same thing as the “Holy Spirit.” PHYSICALLY, his body remains in heaven until the day it descends in global, unmistakable, lightning-like glory. Matthew 24:23 serves as an essential guardrail. Deception does not always look like an open atheist denying God; more often, it looks like a religious teacher holding up a cross, a text, or an altar and claiming they have a localized monopoly on Christ’s physical presence or return. True safety lies in anchoring our souls strictly to the written Word of God and the authentic, scriptural blueprint of His coming. If the manifestation of Christ does not match the universal, cosmic brilliance of cosmic lightning, the Church is commanded to turn away.


Matthew 24:28: “..wheresoever the carcass is..”: This idiom conveys the idea of absolute certainty: You do not need to look for a map to find where a dead carcass is in the desert; you simply look up and see the vultures or eagles (aetoi) circling overhead. The birds are an automatic, inescapable sign of the carcass. Spiritually and historically, wherever there is moral corruption and dead spiritual apostasy (the carcass), the swift, devastating execution of God’s judicial judgement (the eagles/vultures) will inevitably drop out of the sky. In 70AD, the Roman army, whose primarily military banner was the Aquila(Eagle), descended directly upon dead, apostate, Jerusalem. At the end of time, the final wrath of God will fall just as precisely on a spiritually dead world.


Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days…”: Jesus sets a precise, unalterable chronological anchor. The cosmic signs do not occur before the pressure, but right at the grand finale of the tribulation period. “..the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light…” This uses classic OT prophetic language (see Isa 13:10 or Joel 2:31). The physical creation itself will undergo convulsive agony as the light sources of human existence are shut down, plunging the planet into profound darkness just prior to the brilliant arrival of the King of Kings. Symbolically, in ancient near-eastern literature, the sun, moon, and stars represented rulers, nations, and geopolitical powers. For example Joseph’s dreams about the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing down to him (Gen 37:9), or Babylon’s fall: "Behold, the day of the LORD cometh...For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine” (Isa 13:9-10 KJV) or the judgement on Egypt: “And when I shall put thee out, I will cover the heaven, and make the stars thereof dark; I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon shall not give her light” (Eze 32:7 KJV), etc. Hence, Jesus is declaring that the entire established global order, worldly governments, and secular power will completely collapse and be shattered by the arrival of the Kingdom of God.


Matthew 29:30: “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man..”: The context suggests that the “sign” is the unmistakable breakthrough of Jesus Himself. The universe-wide lightning flash of His arrival is the sign that vindicates His Word. “..and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn..”: This is a direct quote from Zechariah 12:10-12. The mourning here is not a holy, repentant sorrow leading to salvation; it is the absolute terror and panic (“men’s hearts failing them for fear”) of a rebellious world that suddenly realizes the God they mocked, denied, and persecuted is real, and He has arrived to execute judgement. “..and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven..”: Jesus intentionally utilizes the language of Daniel 7:13-14. In the OT, riding on the clouds is a visual action reserved exclusively for YHWH (Ps 104:3). By executing this action, Jesus claims to be the same YHWH as in the OT. 


***The glory of the Father and the glory of the Son are not two separate, competing lights. Jesus is the “brightness of His glory, and the express image of His person” (Heb 1:3 KJV). The Father is the invisible, infinite fountain of Spirit; the Son is the visible, physical face of that exact same Spirit. When Jesus descends in Mt 24:30, he does not shine with a secondary, borrowed light. He shines with the Glory of the Father because the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily inside of him (Col 2:9). The very light that blinds the rebellious nations in the raw, unveiled glory of the one true God, breaking through the physical body of Jesus Christ to claim His inheritance over the earth.


Matthew 24:31: “..with a great sound of a trumpet..”: The trumpet (shofar) was used in ancient Israel to assemble the congregation, signal an alarm for war, and announce the year of Jubilee. This corresponds perfectly with Paul’s descriptions of the resurrection and translation of the Church at the ultimate climax of the age (1 Thess 4:16; 1 Cor 15:52). “..and they shall gather together his elect..”: The final harvest of human history takes place. The angels act as the reapers, physically gathering every true believer who endured the fire. “..from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other”: This is a Hebrew idiom meaning the entire global compass: north, south, east, and west. No hidden or forgotten saint will be left behind, whether they are alive on earth or asleep in the grave (“one end of heaven to the other”).


*** Jehovah's Witnesses like to use verses like Mt 24:31, or more specifically 1 Thess 4:16, where Paul says: “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first” (KJV). They reason: (1) Jesus descends; (2) He has “the voice of the archangel”; (3) Therefore Jesus must be the archangel; (4) Since Michael is the only archangel named in Scripture (Jude 9), Jesus must be Michael. Hence, they reduce Jesus from the one true God in the flesh (Jn 1:1; 8:58; 10:30; 20:28; Titus 2:13; Heb 1:8; 1 Jn 5:20; Isa 9:6; Mt 1:23; Col 2:9; etc), to a created angel that does not deserve worship as God. This is a very dangerous teaching as the Bible states that: “ye shall die in your sins: for if ye believe not that I AM [he], ye shall die in your sins” (Jn 8:24 KJV) - Jesus declares himself to be the same I AM and YHWH of the OT over and over throughout Scripture (Jn 8:58; Mt 3:3; Phil 2:10-11; Rev 1:17; 2:8; 22:13; etc), and whoever denies that will die of their sins. Notice how 1 Thess 4:16 never says” The Lord is the archangel.” It only says: “The Lord shall descend.. WITH a shout, WITH the voice of the archangel, WITH the trump of God.” Notice there are three accompanying features: (1) a shout, (2) the voice of the archangel, (3) the trumpet of God. If “with the voice of the archangel” proves Jesus is an archangel, then consistency would require saying that Jesus is a shout & that Jesus is God’s trumpet. Obviously that is not what Paul is saying. This verse describes what accompanies Christ’s coming. “With” does not mean “is.” Christ is coming WITH a shout, WITH the voice of THE archangel (probably Michael accompanying him), WITH the trump of God. The verse distinguishes Christ from the archangel. Paul says: “The Lord himself..”. This emphasizes Christ’s personal appearance. Then he mentions the shout, the archangel’s voice, and God’s trumpet. The grammar naturally distinguishes these. The Bible constantly says that angels accompany Christ on His return: "For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father WITH HIS ANGELS” (Mt 16:27 KJV, also see Mt 25:31, Mk 8:38; 2 Thess 1:7) - if angels accompany Christ, why would it be surprisingly for an archangel’s voice to accompany His coming? Far from being an angel, Jesus commands them (“The Son of man shall send forth his angels..”, Mt 13:41 KJV). Hebrews clearly distinguishes Christ from angels: “Being made so much better THAN THE ANGELS..” (Heb 1:4 KJV) - Christ is not one among angels, He is superior to them. “For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son..” (Heb 1:5 KJV) - God never said this to any angel. If Jesus were Michael, the answer would be: “To Michael.” But the inspired answer is: “None of them.” Then the author writes: “And let all the angels of God worship him” (Heb 1:6 KJV) - the angels worship Christ. An archangel IS STILL an angel. Angels worship Christ, they do not worship one of their own order. Also, we see in Jude that Michael appeals to Jesus in order to rebuke Satan: "Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil... durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, THE LORD REBUKE THEE” (Jude 9 KJV). Jesus does not appeal to anybody, He simply commands and rebukes Himself: "Get thee hence, Satan” (Mt 4:10 KJV); “Jesus rebuked him..” (Mk 1:25 KJV). Jesus possesses inherent authority. Michael, an archangel, does not. Jesus possesses the voice of God, not of an archangel (Jn 1:1; 5:26-29). Jesus is worshipped (Mt 14:33; 28:9; Heb 1:6), angels turn down worship (Rev 19:10). Jesus, being the same YHWH of the OT in the flesh, is the creator of angels: "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven... whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers..." (Col 1:16 KJV). A created archangel cannot be the Creator of all angelic beings.


Matthew 24:32: “..parable of the fig tree..”: In the Middle East, most trees are evergreen, keeping their leaves year-round. The fig tree, however, loses its leaves in the winter and stands bare. “When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves…”: In late spring, the sap rises, the twigs soften (“tender”), and bright green leaves rapidly burst forth. “..ye know that summer is nigh”: Jesus states an obvious fact of nature: you don’t need a calendar to know summer is coming; you just look at the tree. The physical foliage is the undeniable visual warning.


Matthew 24:33: “So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things…”: Jesus applies the natural law to prophecy. The “leaves” are the specific signs he just detailed: the rising of false prophets, the Roman armies surrounding the city, the abomination of desolation, and the localized tribulation pressure. “...know that it is near, even at the doors”: The word “it” can refer to the execution of judgement, the destruction of the city, or the Second Coming of the Son of Man. For the first-century disciples, the trap was set, and the executioner was already standing outside the door.


Matthew 24:34: “Verily I say unto you”: literally means: “Amen, I say to you.” “...This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled”: The Greek word for “generation” is “genea,” which in this specific context refers to the contemporary crowd living at that exact time. Telescoping again, we see: (1) Near Peak (Historical Fulfillment in 70AD): Jesus spoke these words around 30 AD. About 40 years later, the Roman legions under Titus utterly demolished Jerusalem, burned the Temple, and dismantled its stones. The very generation that stood before Jesus, listened to his voice, and rejected his Messiahship lived to see this horrific “all these things” of the localized Judean tribulation come to pass. (2) Taller, Farther Peak (End Times): Prophetically, the word “genea” also carries a dual-fulfillment weight. The specific future generation that sees the final, global end-time signs begin to burst forth like fig leaves will not pass away until the complete cosmic finale and the literal Second Coming are consummated.

Matthew 24:35: "Heaven and earth shall pass away..”: The physical universe (the stars, the planets, the earth, and everything humans perceive as solid, permanent, and unshakeable) is actually temporary (Heb 1:11-12; 2 Peter 3:10). “..but my words shall not pass away”: In the OT, YHWH explicitly declares that His word stands forever while the creation fades (Isa 40:8). By elevating his personal spoken words above the stability of the physical heaven and earth, Jesus explicitly identifies Himself as the same eternal YHWH manifested in the flesh. The Roman Empire would fall, the Temple would crumble, and the cosmos would burn, but the words of Jesus Christ remain completely indestructible. Any false religion, like Catholicism, that teaches that doctrine develops over time (Pope Fancis literally made John Henry Newman a saint & doctor of the church in 2019 for teaching that doctrine develops over time), let it be accursed. Jesus’ Words are God’s Words (Jn 1:1,14; 12:49; 14:24), and His teachings DO NOT CHANGE NOR DEVELOP OVER TIME, THEY ARE ETERNAL:  “But though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, let him be accursed” (Gal 1:8 KJV), always “earnestly contend for the faith which was ONCE delivered unto the saints” (Jude 1:3 KJV). 


Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour..”: In v.34 Jesus discusses all the visible signs, but now he shifts to the specific time of the end of the age and final judgement. “..knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven..”: Neither human intellect, prophetic calculation, nor high angelic intelligence in the heavenly realm possesses the calendar date for the end. “..but my Father only”: “Father” refers to “YHWH”, to “Holy Spirit”, to “God”, they are all interchangeable. It does not, however, mean “Son” - the Father IS NOT the Son (that would be “modalism”), rather, the Father IS IN the Son. The term “God-the-Son” is unbiblical. The “Son” refers to the human born of Mary in which the Father dwelt (Col 2:9-10; 2 Cor 5:19; Jn 14:8-9). The “Son” is useless by himself. The Father (God) is the one who glorifies the human body to be His Son & eternal visible image. When we compare Mt 24:36 with its direct parallel passage, Mark 13:32, the phrasing becomes even more explicit and startling: "But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, NEITHER THE SON, but the Father” (KJV). Trinitarians often struggle with this verse because, under their model of three co-equal, co-eternal “persons” in the Godhead, if the Son is a distinct divine person equal to the Father, he must possess eternal omniscience at all times. If “God the Son” lacks knowledge that “God the Father” possesses, their co-equality is broken. Trinitarian theologians will try to use Phil 2:6-8 (“Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross”, KJV) to teach that although Jesus was fully God (as pre-incarnate Jesus, as the 2nd divine person of the Trinity, not as the eternal Father), when he became a man, he VOLUNTARILY restricted the use of certain divine attributes. But under scrutiny, this makes absolutely no sense. For example, say God-the-Son KNOWS ALL, but his human nature DOES NOT KNOW ALL. Did he cease to be God since he is no longer omniscient? As a human that DOES NOT KNOW ALL, how can he return to KNOWING ALL if he no longer possesses the divine omniscience or power to revert things? The Son literally died, does that mean that God-the-Son can die? Can God die? The Son GREW is stature & wisdom(Lk 2:52), how does God grow is stature & wisdom? Either you know everything, or you don’t. It is impossible to alternate between knowing everything and not knowing. The answer lies in the Oneness of God: where the Father is the one true God who is Spirit: “And this is life eternal, that they might know thee THE ONLY TRUE GOD, and Jesus Christ(the human, image, and temple of the only true God)” (Jn 17:3 KJV). In Jesus, there are TWO (not three) witnesses (Jn 8:17-18): (1) the Father and (2) the human Son. The Father never ceases to be omniscient, and the human is never omniscient UNTIL the human body is glorified by the Father as His eternal image. The two are one (Jn 10:30) - notice it’s two, not three. There’s more than the Father in Jesus, there’s humanity added to the Spirit of the Father, that’s why the Greek word for “one” in Jn 10:30 is “hen,” which is the neuter form of one conveying a UNITY of distinct individuals: one fully human (with his own human spirit, human will, and human consciousness  - a real authentic human being, the second Adam), & one as the eternal Spirit (with His own divine Spirit, divine Will, and divine consciousness). When Jesus doesn’t know all things, it’s because the human doesn’t know all things, but when Jesus does have some supernatural knowledge before his glorification, it’s because the divine Spirit of the Father reveals it to the human. Jesus himself declares: “ALL things(authority, knowledge, revelation) are delivered unto me of my Father” (Mt 11:27 KJV) & “I thank thee, O FATHER, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast REVEALED them unto babes” (Mt 11:25 KJV). At the end of age, the mediator role, as the human, will end & completely fuse with the Father so God may be all in all: “And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all” (1 Cor 15:28 KVJ). The important thing is to realize that Jesus is not a second person of the Trinity incarnated, rather Jesus is THE ONE GOD who is Father of us all come in the flesh. That’s why when you see Jesus, you see the Father(Jn 12:45;14:9). That’s why when you know Jesus, you know the Father (Jn 14:7). The “unity” of God is not between distinct divine persons, but rather it’s between the eternal Spirit and its visible, human temple. 


*** Since Trinitarians heavily rely on Phil 2:5-8 to teach that Jesus is a second divine person that came in the flesh rather than the entire Godhead, I will dissect the text from a Oneness perspective to show that it does not teach Trinitarianism. The full text reads: “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.” (Phil 2:5-11 KJV). Phil 2:5-11 from a Oneness perspective: 
(Verse 5): “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus”: since the mind in you, is the same also in Christ Jesus, here it is referring to the HUMAN mind of Christ Jesus, not the eternal divine Spirit that is God. The focus is not on the transcendent nature of God, which we humans cannot duplicate, but on the attitude and conduct of the man Jesus, which we can imitate. 
(Verse 6): “Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God”: there are two forms: (1) the form of God (a divine Spirit), that only God can have (Isa 43:10;45:5), & (2) the form of a servant (a human), that we all have. Jesus is “in the form of God” because God-in-the-flesh is STILL the same as God-before-the-flesh. The man Jesus had access to the divine Spirit “without limit” (Jn 3:34 BSB) (the same as God), but while on Earth, he decided to not use his divine prerogatives (“thought it not robbery to be equal with God”). The word “equal” comes from the Greek “isos”, and it means: “equal” or “the same.” For example: “God gave them the SAME(isos) gift..” (Acts 17:11 BSB). So essentially what v.6 is saying is: “even though the man Jesus was still God, he did not consider being the same as God(omniscient, omnipresent, omnipotent) something to be used to his own advantage” (v.6); this is very close to how the NIV actually translated it: “Who, being in the very nature God, did not consider equality with God something to be used to his own advantage” (v.6 NIV). The use of “equal” does not require Jesus to be a secondary divine person. If it did, the Bible would have a contradiction, for God has no equal and there is none like Him (Isa 46:5,9). If “equal with” indicates a distinct divine person, then Jesus would not merely be a distinct person from the Father, but a distinct person from “God” altogether. So here, what we see is the distinction between the human and the divine Spirit: although the human born of Mary possessed the nature & identity of God by: (1) being Immanuel - “God with us” (Mt 1:23); (2) being the “express image of His person(hypostasis)” (Heb 1:3): notice there is only one invisible divine hypostasis(person), of whom the man Jesus is the image of (he is not a second divine person, but the visible image of the one divine person); (3) being a man “FULL of the Holy Spirit(God)” (Lk 4:1): “For in him dwelleth ALL the fulness of the Godhead bodily” (Col 2:9) & (4) having access to this divine Spirit “without limit” (Jn 3:34 BSB); yet, he humbled himself & willingly gave up his divine prerogatives & privileges by accepting his human limitations. Since the Father (the divine Spirit) had given EVERYTHING to the human Son (“All things are delivered unto me of my Father..”, Mt 11:27 KJV), at any moment, the man Jesus could have used His divine glory, as in the transfiguration, but instead he veiled his glory, the Father’s glory (Jn 8:54 BSB), and displayed the ordinary human appearance as the Son of Man.
(Verse 7): “But made himself of no reputation(‘emptied himself’ BSB), and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men”: Trinitarians see this “emptying” as pre-incarnate God-the-Son giving up all his divine attributes to become a man totally dependent on the Father. But if that was the case, then God-the-Son would literally cease to be God, since you cannot be “God” without omniscience (the Son did not know all things), omnipresence (the human had to physically walk), or omnipotence (the human was physically weak & literally died). Rather, this “emptying” occurred when the human, as the suffering servant, “poured out his soul unto death” (Isa 53:12 KJV). His “emptying” includes his entire human ministry. The human humbled himself, laid aside any divine privileges(his unlimited access to the Spirit of the Father) and accepted his mission of being birthed in Mary’s womb and sent out into the world as a suffering servant(“taking upon the form of a servant”) under his human limitations (“in the likeness of men”). The man Jesus always knew his purpose since he was a kid. At 12 years old, he was already saying things like: “Didn’t you know I had to be in my Father’s house?” (Lk 2:49 KJV) - fully aware of his earthly mission.  This does not mean that the Son was pre-existent, for the Father prophesied: “I WILL(future tense) be to him a Father; and he SHALL(future tense) be to me a Son” (Heb 1:5 KJV) - there was a time when the Father was not the Father of the human, and the human was not the Son of the Father yet: “But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son(from the womb, out into the world, the same way He “sent” John the Baptist in Jn 1:6), made of a woman, made under the law” (Gal 4:4 KJV) - notice it cannot refer to a pre-incarnate Son as there was no mother then. This cannot refer to modalism either(believing that God-the-Father ceased to be the Father and became God-the-Son), since God continues to be Spirit in the NT (Jn 4:24); so “took upon him the form of a servant” DOES NOT mean that the Spirit became flesh, rather that the man Jesus humbly accepted his role as the suffering servant.
(Verse 8): “And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross”: as an authentic human being, with his own human will (Mt 26:39), human spirit (Lk 23:46), human soul and human consciousness (Mt 26:38; Jn 12:27), he humbled himself and became obedient to God-the-Father unto death. The man Jesus lived a sinless life, something no one else has ever been able to do, not even Mary (“For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God”, Rom 3:23 KJV). That’s why, as a sinless man, he is the only one able to come close to the perfect, holy glory of God on our behalf: “For there is one(heis: singular masculine one) God, and one mediator between God and men, the MAN(not a 2nd divine person) Christ Jesus” (1 Tim 2:5 KJV). If the human were a second divine person, we’d need yet another sinless mediator between us and that divine person since God separates from sin (“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear”, Isa 59:2 KJV). The sinless man Jesus is our ONLY way to the Father: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me” (Jn 14:6 KJV) - because he is the Father veiled in flesh (Jn 14:8-9).
(Verse 9): “Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name”: God (the Father, YHWH, the Holy Spirit) exalted the human Son (not another God, since God does not need exaltation), and gave him the name ABOVE EVERY NAME: “Jesus” (which means YHWH-Saves). Recall that where the “name” of God is, there is God Himself (Deut 12:5; 1 Kings 9:3). For a Trinitarian, “Jesus” is simply the human name that God-the-Son was given on Earth, so they teach that the name given to the Son in this verse is “Lord,” not “Jesus” (MacArthur Study notes on Phil 2:9); and for a Jehovah’s Witness, since “Jehovah” is supposed to be the name ABOVE EVERY NAME, they manipulate this verse and render it as: “God exalted him to a superior position and kindly gave him the name that is above every OTHER name” (Phil 2:9 NWT, Jehovah’s Witnesses Bible) - notice they add the word “OTHER” since “Jesus” cannot be above the name of “Jehovah” (recall that “Jehovah” is a made up name that consists of the tetragrammaton plus the vowels of the Hebrew word for “Lord” [Adonai], hence: “YHWH” + “A” + “o” + “a” = YAHoWaH or Jehovah. This name was created by the Masoretic Jews around the 6th century in order to prevent themselves from ever taking God’s name in vain. It was never intended to be pronounced as written, but it was a reminder of: “When you see YHWH, read ‘Adonai’ “). However, both Trinitarians and Jehovah’s Witnesses are wrong. The name of “Jesus” is the ONLY name given to men under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:10,12). It is the full revelation of YHWH in the NT, since it describes what He is going to do: save us from our sins (Mt 1:21). It’s the name prophesied about: “And the Lord shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be ONE Lord, and HIS NAME ONE” (Zech 14:9 KJV). When Mary was overshadowed by the Holy Spirit (baby Jesus’ Father), Mary was specifically instructed to name the baby “Jesus” because “he shall save his people from their sins” (Mt 1:21 KJV). His name literally means what he was going to do: “YHWH-saves” us from our sins. The human born of Mary INHERITED (“he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name,” Heb 1:4 KJV) the name of the Father. The word “inherited” means that the name belonged to the Father before being passed down to him. That’s why Jesus could say: “Holy FATHER, protect them BY YOUR NAME, THE NAME YOU GAVE ME” (Jn 17:11 BSB). This is also why Jesus said in Mt 28:18 that ALL AUTHORITY had been given unto him (from the divine spirit to the human), therefore go and baptize in the name of other divine people…. Of course not! Rather, he said: “All authority has been given to ME(Jesus)” hence go into all the world and make disciples by baptizing them in MY NAME(Emperor Constantine’s historian Eusebius cited Mt 28:18 as "Go, and make disciples of all the nations in MY NAME" before the Council of Nicaea of 325AD), which is the singular name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. This is why in the parallel passages of the Great Commission (Mk 16:15-18; Lk 24:45-49 & Acts 1:8;2:38) it is more clearly stated that it’s the name of “Jesus” by which we carry out the Great Commission. We see the three titles applied to Jesus in Isaiah 9:6: “unto us a (1)SON is given… and his name will be called… (2)COUNSELLOR(Spirit)... everlasting (3)FATHER” (KJV). The human Jesus carried the name of the Father (YHWH-Saves = “Jesus”), that is why Jesus said: “I will declare THY NAME unto my brethren” (Heb 2:12 KJV) - and he only declared the name of “Jesus.” He also said: “I am come in my Father’s NAME” (Jn 5:43 KJV); and “the works that I do in my Father’s NAME, they bear witness of me” (Jn 10:25 KJV); & “I have manifested THY NAME unto the men” (Jn 17:6 KJV) and he only manifested the name of “Jesus”; and “I have declared unto them THY NAME” (Jn 17:26 KJV) and he only declared the name of “Jesus”; etc etc. This is why we will see only ONE on the throne (Rev 4:2), & this “ONE” is described as two: “the throne of God(the invisible Spirit of the Father) AND of the Lamb(the visible image of the Son)... and they shall see HIS FACE(one face); and HIS NAME(one name: ‘Jesus’) shall be in their foreheads” (Rev 22:3-4 KJV) because the two are ONE (“I and my Father are one,” Jn 10:30), creating a perfect unity of humanity and divinity, an invisible Spirit and a visible temple, a unity of two, not three. And since the Father of the man Jesus is the “Holy Spirit” (“that which is CONCEIVED in her is of the Holy Ghost”, Mt 1:20), of course the Spirit’s name will also be “YHWH-Saves”: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send IN MY NAME(Jesus)” (Jn 14:26 KJV) & “But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the SPIRIT OF CHRIST, he is none of his” (Rom 8:9 KJV), because “the Lord(Jesus) is that Spirit” (2 Cor 3:17). That is why “Holy Spirit” is constantly used interchangeably with “Spirit of Jesus” (Acts 16:6-7 CT, see also: 1 Pet 1:10-11; Gal 4:6; Jn 14:17-18; 16:7; Mt 28:20; Phil 1:19). This is also why every single apostle obeyed Jesus’ Great Commission by baptizing explicitly in the name of Jesus, not in a vague, nameless Trinity (Acts 2:38; 8:12; 8:16; 10:48; 19:5; 22:16; Rom 6:3-4; 1 Cor 1:13-14; Gal 3:27; Col 2:12; Js 2:7), with the name of “Jesus” being orally invoked at baptism (Acts 22:16; Js 2:7 CSB, AMPC) and rebaptizing those who had been baptized in any other way (Acts 19:3-5), since “Jesus” is the only saving name given to men (Acts 4:12).
(Verse 10): “That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;”: to confirm everything explained above, the name given to the Son is “Jesus”, not “Lord” (as Trinitarians try to teach). Here it says that every knee will bow to the name of Jesus, yet in the OT YHWH says: “there is no God else beside me(YHWH); a just God and a Saviour; there is none beside me(YHWH). Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else. That unto me(YHWH) EVERY KNEE SHALL BOW, every tongue shall swear” (Isa 45:21-23 KJV) - notice the speaker is YHWH, who says “I am God, and there is none else.” He swears by Himself because there is no greater authority (“God made promises… because He could swear by no greater, He sware by Himself” Heb 6:13 KJV). Yet the prophecy is fulfilled in Jesus because Jesus is the same YHWH of the OT in the flesh.
(Verse 11): “And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.”: Calling Jesus “Lord” could mean two things: (1) that
 Jesus, as God in the flesh, is the sovereign master and owner of everything; and (2) Trinitarians like to read “Lord” as “YHWH”. The Greek Septuagint (LXX) translated “YHWH” as “Lord” in order to respect the divine name and prevent taking it in vain. So here you would see two YHWH’s: Jesus who is Lord(YHWH), and God the Father who is YHWH as well. Two distinct divine persons sharing the divine essence of God (YHWH). However, this interpretation would contradict the OT, which explicitly states that YHWH is one, not two nor three: “The LORD our God is one LORD(YHWH)” (Deut 6:4 KJV); “the LORD(YHWH) He is God; there is none else beside Him” (Deut 4:35 KJV); “O LORD(YHWH) God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God beside thee” (2 Sam 7:22 KJV); “I the LORD(YHWH), the first, and with the last; I am HE(not they)” (Isa 41:4 KJV); “I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God” (Isa 44:6 KJV); “Before me there was no God formed, neither shall there be after me. I, even I, am the LORD(YHWH); and beside me there is no saviour” (Isa 43:10-11 KJV); etc etc. YHWH clearly says He is one, yet Trinitarians will take this “one” to mean a “unity of divine persons.” As support, they will use verses that sound like there are two YHWHs. For example: “Then the LORD(YHWH) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD(YHWH) out of heaven” (Gen 19:24 KJV). However, this conclusion lacks information. First, Jesus cites Deut 6:4 in Mk 12:29, and when he says “the LORD is ONE(heis),” he uses the Greek word for SINGULAR MASCULINE ONE that demands one person, that is why the Amplified Bible explicitly adds “one person” in Gal 3:20: “God is [only] one(heis) Person” (AMPC). The reason it sounds like there are two YHWH’s is because in Hebrew, they tend to repeat the subject in order to emphasize who is the one doing the action, in this case YHWH. We can see another example of this in 1 Kings 8:1: “Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel…unto king Solomon in Jerusalem” (KJV) - notice it sounds like there are two Solomons, but no one serious will ever try to argue that there are two of them. Likewise, although sometimes it sounds like there are two YHWH’s, remember that YHWH is omnipresent and that the Hebrews are simply emphasizing the one doing the action, not trying to teach that there are multiple YHWH’s. Another common tactic is to point out that the Hebrew word for God is “Elohim,” which is a plural word, so Trinitarians would argue that “Elohim” is plural because there are multiple divine persons in the Godhead. This conclusion, again, lacks information. The Hebrews would use plural words to describe singular things that are overwhelming, too great, too large, or too powerful. For example, the Hebrew words for water, heaven, sky, life, youth, virginity, or a large animal like a behemoth, are all plural words describing singular things. Also, if “Elohim” makes God a Triune God, then the golden calf would also be Triune, since the SINGULAR golden calf is also called “Elohim”(Ex 32:4). Not just that, but every single pagan god: Baal is Elohim (Judges 6:31); Dagon is Elohim (Judges 16:23); etc etc. A third Trinitarian argument to argue for a plurality of YHWH’s are verses like Gen 1:26, where God says: “Let US make man in OUR image” (KJV). They argue that the “US” here must refer to God-the-Son, God-the-Spirit and God-the-Father. This, too, lacks information. God already said He is one, first & last, etc. so there are plenty of alternate better explanations for the plural “US.” First, the very next verse reads: “So God created man in HIS own image” (Gen 1:27 KJV). Why would He go back to singular if He was Triune? The answer is simple: because YHWH(God) is not Triune, and the singular masculine pronouns and verbs attest to that. Second, God was most likely addressing His heavenly court, as Scripture constantly describes God surrounded by angels and other heavenly beings (1 Kings 22:19; Job 1:6  ; Isa 6:1-8), and we know that they were present at creation (Job 38:4, 7). Perhaps God was speaking as a plural of majesty or deliberation, how some monarchs would speak in the plural as: “We have decided…” For example, Daniel told King Nebuchadnezzar: “We will tell the interpretation thereof before the king,” even though Daniel alone proceeded to give the interpretation (Daniel 2:36), or when King Artaxerxes referred to himself in the plural in Ezra 7:24. Another possible explanation is like how we say: “Let’s do this!” which means: “Let US do this!” but it’s just us doing the action alone. Another possible explanation is God speaking to Himself, or to the counsel of His own Will (Eph 1:11). Or perhaps He was talking to the future Son, since God “calls those things which be not as though they were” (Rom 4:17 KJV), or perhaps God was using His foreknowledge of the Son (Jn 1:1,14; Acts 2:23; 1 Pet 1:18-20; Rev 13:8). So many possible explanations, but the least likely explanation is the Trinity. “...to the glory of God the Father”: Isaiah says every knee bows to YHWH, and Paul says every knee bows to Jesus the Lord(YHWH). Hence, honoring the Son, you honor the divine Spirit of YHWH (“to the glory of God the Father)”. John tells us that: “For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son: That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him” (Jn 5:22-23 KJV) - why would you honor a human the same as God if not because they are the same one God? Jesus said it himself: “If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him… he that hath seen me hath seen the Father” (Jn 14:7,9 KJV) - when you bow down to Jesus, you bow down to the one eternal YHWH of the OT in the flesh.


Matthew 24:37: “But as the days of Noe[Noah] were..”: Jesus explicitly picks a historic, global catastrophe as the direct type and shadow for his physical return. He does not compare his coming to an era of global revival or widespread political peace, but to an era marked by profound spiritual apathy, wickedness, and sudden judgement. “...so shall also the coming of the Son of man be”: The structural pattern of Noah’s flood (long warning, absolute indifference by the masses, sudden supernatural judgement, and immediate separation) is the exact blueprint for “the coming”(Parousia).


Matthew 24:38: “..eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage..”: Notice what Jesus lists here. He does not highlight monstrous crimes like murder or idolatry (though Gen 6:5 notes those were present); he highlights normal, legitimate, everyday human routines. The deadly sin of Noah’s generation was not merely gross wickedness; it was complete spiritual blindness caused by earthly absorption. They were so consumed with living, social maneuvering, business, and pleasure that they completely ignored the giant wooden ark being built in their face. They lived as if tomorrow would always look like today.


Matthew 24:39: “And knew not..”: It was not that they hadn’t been warned, as Noah was a “preacher of righteousness” for decades (2 Peter 2:5). They “knew not” because they voluntarily refused to believe. They mistook God’s long-suffering patience for approval or non-existence. “..until the flood came, and took them all away..”: When the rain started, the door of the ark was already sealed by God Himself (Gen 7:16). There was no second chance, no extended discussion, and no late entry. The judgement was total and immediate. “..so shall also the coming of the Son of man be”: Just like the floodgate snapped shut, the final arrival of Christ will cut human history in two with absolute finality.


Matthew 24:40: “Then shall two be in the field..”: Jesus shifts to a workplace setting: two men performing the same heavy, outdoor manual labor side-by-side. “..the one shall be taken, and the other left”: On the surface, both men look identical. They wear the same clothes, work the same dirt, and earn the same wage. But spiritually, one belongs to the Kingdom of God, and the other is anchored to the earth. A sudden, supernatural divide occurs in a microsecond. The “taken” could mean two things: (1) In verse 39, the flood came and “took them [the wicked] all away.” Following the exact grammar of Noah’s analogy, the ones who are “taken” are swept away in divine judgement, while the ones “left” remain safe in the kingdom of earth (the ark). (2) The Greek word for “taken” (paralambano) literally means “to take alongside to oneself with affection”, and this is the exact word that Jesus uses in John 14:3 (“I will come again, and receive[paralambano] you unto myself”). In this light, the elect are supernaturally “taken” by the angels to meet the Lord, while the wicked are “left” behind for destruction. In either interpretation, the core truth is unshakeable: The coming of Christ brings an instantaneous, irreversible separation between the saved and the lost.


Matthew 24:41: “Two women shall be grinding at the mill…”: This describes domestic, home-based labor. In ancient Judea, two women sat facing each other, turning a heavy circular stone to grind grain for the morning bread. “..one shall be taken, and the other left”: Neither close family ties, shared domestic responsibilities, nor physical proximity can save a person. Salvation is intensely individual. You cannot enter the kingdom on the coattails of a godly spouse, parent, or coworker. 


Matthew 24:42: “Watch therefore..”: This is the imperative climax of the entire chapter. The Greek word is “gregoreite,” meaning to stay awake, remain alert, and maintain constant spiritual vigilance. “..for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come”: Because the date cannot be calculated by charts or calendar predictions, readiness cannot be delayed to “later.” Readiness must be a continuous, present-tense state of being.


*** Many people treat salvation like an insurance policy they can secure at the last minute. But Jesus warns that his coming will occur on an ordinary, unannounced day, while people are plowing fields, grinding flour, making plans, and living in mundane routine. Spiritual alertness (“Watch therefore”) requires three active realities: (1) Spiritual Sobriety: Refusing to let the legitimate cares, pleasures, and routines of this world dull out hunger for God (Lk 21:34). (2) Continuous Obedience: Walking firmly in the Apostolic blueprint of Acts 2:38, living a consecrated, holy life daily so that whenever the trumpet sounds, our lamps are trimmed and burning. (3) Expectant Waiting: Living with the daily awareness that Jesus could break through the clouds at any moment.


Matthew 24:43: “But know this..” Jesus commands focused mental engagement. He uses an everyday illustration of home security to expose human inconsistency. “..if the goodman of the house had known in what watch…”: The “goodman” refers to the master or head of the household. In the ancient world, the night was divided into four distinct guard shifts (“watches”). “..the thief would come, he would have watched..”: A homeowner who receives advance notice of a burglary does not go to sleep; he stays alert during that specific hour. “...and would not have suffered his house to be broken up”: Ancient homes were often made of sun-dried mud brick, allowing a thief to literally dig or break through (diorysso) the wall unnoticed under the cover of darkness. The lesson is sharp: people exercise extreme diligence to protect physical possessions, yet often treat their eternal souls with total carelessness.


Matthew 24:44: “Therefore be ye also ready..”: Notice the imperative. Readiness is not a passive emotion; it is an active, ongoing state of spiritual preparation. “..for in such an hour as ye think not..”: Like a thief, no one knows the hour of the Lord’s return, but a believer must be ready at all times: both, in case he comes sooner than expected (vv.43-51), or in case he comes after than expected (Mt 25:1-13).


Matthew 24:45: The primary duty assigned to the “faithful and wise servant” is to feed the master’s household with proper nourishment at the proper time. This highlights the responsibility of ministers and leaders to consistently proclaim the uncompromised Word of God, dispensing truth that sustains the Church.


Matthew 24:46: “Blessed is that servant..”: The beatitude is pronounced not on the servant who started well, but on the one who finishes well. “..shall find so doing”: Christianity is not a religion of past achievements; it is a life of present consistency. The Lord rewards active duty, not idle memory.


Matthew 24:47: “...he shall make him ruler over all his goods”: Temporary faithfulness in managing God’s earthly household yields eternal authority and stewardship in the Kingdom to come: “Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities” (Lk 19:17 KJV). 


Matthew 24:48: “But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart..”: Apostasy rarely begins with an immediate public renunciation of faith; it begins as a quiet, internal shift in the heart (“shall say in his heart”). “My lord delayeth his coming..”: This is the root toxin of spiritual backsliding. The moment a person stops expecting Christ’s imminent return, their lifestyle begins to decompose. Presuming upon time leads directly to carnal indulgence(sexual immortality, drugs, mistreatment of others, etc).


Matthew 24:49: “And shall begin to smite his fellowservants..”: Once the fear of the Lord and the expectancy of his return vanish, internal abuse sets in. This manifests as spiritual tyranny, harshness, biting words, and division among believers. “...and to eat and drink with the drunken”: The evil servant lowers his standards and joins hands with the world. He abandons consecration, holiness, and sobriety, fully indulging in worldly pleasures and compromise.


Matthew 24:50: “The lord of that servant shall come..”: The delay was an illusion. The master’s return is fixed, sovereign, and inescapable. “...when he looketh not for him..”: Judgement strikes at the peak of the servant’s self-indulgence and false security.


Matthew 24:51: “And shall cut him asunder..”: The Greek word for “asunder” is “dichotomeo,” literally meaning “to cut into two pieces.” It represents the severe execution of divine justice for hypocrisy and treason. “...appoint him his portion with the hypocrites..”: The servant’s ultimate tragedy is that despite wearing the uniform of the master’s household, his heart belonged to the wicked. He is assigned to the exact place reserved for pretenders. “..there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth”: A description of absolute despair, conscious torment, and eternal regret over wasted opportunity.
Matthew 25
Matthew 25:1: Jesus gives the Parable of the Ten Virgins. “Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened..”: The word “Then” links this directly to the sudden arrival of the Son of Man at the end of the age (Mt 24:44,50). “...unto ten virgins..”: In ancient Near Eastern weddings, the bridegroom would travel to the bride’s home, finalize the covenant, and lead a nighttime procession back to his home for the feast. The bridesmaid (“virgins”) waited along the route to join the procession with lit lamps. The “Virgins” represent professors of faith, those who have separated themselves from the outward corruption of the world and claim allegiance to Christ. The “Bridegroom” represents Jesus Christ himself. The “Lamps” represent the outward profession of faith, the visible vessel, or church membership.


Matthew 25:2: “And five of them were wise, and five were foolish”: On the surface, all ten look identical. All ten are called virgins, all ten hold lamps, all ten are in the right location, and all ten expect the bridegroom. The critical divide is not external appearance, but internal wisdom (“phronimos”) versus spiritual foolishness (“moros”).


Matthew 25:3: “..took no oil with them..”: The foolish had just enough oil in their wicks to produce a brief temporary flame for the moment. However, they carried no extra reserve in separate vessels. They were content with a superficial experience: enough religion to look the part, but no deep, sustaining reservoir.


Matthew 25:4: “..took oil in their vessels with their lamps”: The wise understood that the bridegroom might not arrive on their preferred timeline. They made preparations for endurance. Throughout Scripture, oil consistently symbolizes the Holy Spirit (Anointing, infilling, and sanctification). The “Lamp” is the human vessel/profession (“The spirit of man is the candle of the LORD,” Prov 20:27). The oil in the vessel represents the deep, continuous infilling and abiding presence of the Holy Spirit (“..be filled with the Spirit”, Eph 5:18). The wise had an internal, continuous relationship with God, not just an external container.


Matthew 25:5: “While the bridegroom tarried…”: Jesus hints again at a delay. The test of true spirituality is not how high you jump when the excitement is hot, but how you stand during the quiet delay. “..they all slumbered and slept”: Notice that both the wise and foolish physically slept. This is not a condemnation of physical sleep or routine life; it highlights that human beings must live, work, and rest in this world. The difference was that when the crisis hit, the wise had an internal reserve that the foolish lacked.


Matthew 25:6: “And at midnight..”: Midnight represents the darkest, most unexpected, and humanly helpless hour. “...there was a cry made..”: The midnight cry corresponds to the trumpet of God and the shout of the archangel (1 Thess 4:16). The time for preparation is officially over; the bridegroom has arrived.


Matthew 25:7: “...trimmed their lamps”: Trimming a lamp meant scraping away the burnt carbon from the end of the wick so the flame could burn bright and clean. Every virgin scrambled to inspect their spiritual state. 


Matthew 25:8: “..Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out”: The crisis exposed their bankruptcy. The foolish realized that a borrowed reputation, a godly family, or a past experience cannot sustain a soul in the final judgement. Salvation is personal. The Spiritual oil (the personal infilling of the Holy Spirit and the personal walk of holiness) CANNOT BE TRANSFERRED or borrowed. You cannot buy oil on credit at midnight. 


Matthew 25:9: “..Not so, lest there be not enough for us and you..”: This is not selfishness; it is a spiritual reality. No human has a surplus of grace or righteousness to give to another. Every individual must possess their own relationship with God. “...go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves”: Salvation is free, but consecration costs everything. Isaiah 55:1 and Revelation 3:18 call us to “buy” gold tried in the fire and white raiment through personal surrender, prayer, and devotion. Recall the man who found the hidden treasure in a field and “selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field” (Mt 13:44 KJV); or the merchant who found the most valuable pearl, and “went and sold all that he had, and bought it” (Mt 13:46 KJV). Accepting Christ’s free gift means giving up all of our sinful baggage: “if any man will come after me, let him DENY HIMSELF, and take up his cross, and follow me” (Mt 16:24 KJV).


Matthew 25:10: “And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came..”: Late preparation is not preparation at all. “...and they that were ready went in with him..”: Readiness is the sole requirement for entry. “..and the door was shut”: This is one of the most sobering phrases in the Gospels. Just as God shut the door of Noah’s ark (Gen 7:16), the door of grace will eventually slam shut with absolute finality. Once closed, no amount of bargaining can open it.


Matthew 25:11: “Afterward came also the other virgins..”: They returned with their purchased oil, but it was too late. “...saying, Lord, Lord, open to us”: They use the covenant language (“Lord, Lord”), proving they were not open atheists or pagan strangers; they were church-goers who assumed they were safe until the very moment the door locked.


Matthew 25:12: “Verily I say unto you, I know you not”: This echoes Mt 7:21-23. The fundamental flaw of the foolish virgins was a lack of intimate relationship (ginosko). They had the religion, the lamp, and the association, but they did not have the indwelling Spirit of the Bridegroom.


Matthew 25:13: “Watch therefore…”: The structural conclusion of the parable. True “watching” is not sitting on a hilltop staring at the sky; it is ensuring that your vessel is continuously filled with the Holy Spirit and your life is lived in unbroken readiness for His arrival. Having a lamp without oil is having “a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof” (2 Tim 3:5 KJV). Romans 8:9 states: “Now if any man have not the SPIRIT OF CHRIST, he is none of his.” The oil is not optional luxury equipment, it is the vital substance that keeps the lamp burning through the midnight hour. 


Matthew 25:14: Jesus now gives the Parable of the Talents. “For the kingdom of heaven is as a man traveling into a far country…”: The “man” represents Jesus Christ, whose ascension into heaven marked a period of physical absence from the earth. “..who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods”: The servants do not own the property; they are managers (stewards). Everything a believer possesses (life, time, gospel truth, spiritual gifts, material wealth) belongs entirely to the Master.


Matthew 25:15: “..gave five talents..two.. one..” : A “talent” (talanton) was not a small coin, but a massive weight of silver or gold, equivalent to roughly 20 years of common laborer’s wages. Even the “one talent” was a life-changing fortune. “...to every man according to his several ability..”: God is sovereign and realistic. He does not distribute gifts equally, but He tailors the entrustment to match each individual’s capacity. God never demands a yield beyond what He equips a person to bear.


Matthew 25:16-17: “went and traded… made them other five..”: Both servants responded with immediate action, industriousness, and faith. They took spiritual risks, invested their labor into the Master’s business, and doubled their principal.


Matthew 25:18: “...went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money”: The third servant did not steal the money, spend it on wild living, or destroy it. His sin was PASSIVE NEGLECT and SPIRITUAL SLOTHFULNESS. He buried the Master’s wealth in the dirt of earthly self-interest. 


Matthew 25:19: “After a long time..”: Once again, Jesus signals that the Second Coming wil not happen immediately; there is an extended interim period testing the endurance and faithfulness of His followers. “...and reckoneth with them”: There is an inescapable day of account. Every steward will stand before the judgement seat of Christ to answer for how they managed what was placed in their hands (“For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad,” 2 Cor 5:10 KJV).


Matthew 25:20-23: “Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord”: Notice that the praise given to the two-talen servant (v.23) is word-for-word identical to the praise given to the five-talent servant (v.21). The Master does not evaluate us based on raw output compared to others, but on faithfulness relative to capacity. Earthly stewardship is merely a testing ground. Faithfulness in “a few things” in this life qualifies a believer for cosmic authority (“ruler over many things”) in the coming Kingdom. 


Matthew 25:24: “I knew thee that thou art an hard man…”: The slothful servant excused his laziness by slandering the Master’s character, calling Him an exactor, unreasonable, and harsh (skleros). False theology always produces spiritual paralysis. When a person views God as an exacting tyrant rather than a gracious King, they withdraw from kingdom service in fear. 


Matthew 25:25: “lo, there thou hast that is thine”: The servant arrogantly presents the original, multiplied talent, as if returning the bare principal without interest was acceptable. He mistook preservation for stewardship.


Matthew 25:26-27: “Thou wicked and slothful servant..”: The Master exposes the servant’s excuse. Sloth (okneros, indolence/laziness) is not a harmless character flaw in the Kingdom of God; it is explicitly condemned as wickedness. “..thou newest that I reap where I sowed not…”: The Master turns the servant’s own words back to him: ‘If you truly believed I was demanding, that should have driven you to be even more cautious and at least deposit the money with bankers (“exchangers”) to collect passive interest!’ He failed even to do the absolute minimum.


Matthew 25:28: “Take therefore the talent from him..”: Kingdom stewardship is an “use it or lose it” reality. Spiritual gifts, opportunities, and light that are actively deployed will compound into greater grace and authority. But those that are neglected and buried will ultimately be revoked and transferred to those who are faithful. 


Matthew 25:29: “For unto every one that hath shall be given… but from his that hath not shall be taken away..”: This verse is not teaching that God arbitrarily makes rich people richer and poor people poorer. In the parable, “having” and “not having” refer primarily to what a person does with what God has entrusted to him. In this context, “he that hath” means the person who possesses something from God and faithfully receives, uses, develops, and acts upon it. The faithful servants “had” in the sense that they had faithful stewardship. They did not merely possess the talents, they put them to use for their master. Therefore, those who faithfully use what God gives them will be entrusted with more. The principle is that faithful use leads to greater responsibility, greater fruitfulness, and ultimately greater reward. The parable emphasizes stewardship and accountability rather than material wealth. The servant that “hat not” did have one talent, yet Jesus says that he will lose even what he has. The meaning is that the servant had the talent PHYSICALLY, but did not possess the faithfulness, fruitfulness, or obedient response that the talent was meant to produce. The principle is: What is faithfully used grows; what is neglected, rejected, or buried is eventually lost. This is true in ordinary life as well. If someone refuses to use or develop an ability, that ability may diminish. The “talents” were literally large units of money in the parable, but they can represent everything God entrusts to a person: knowledge of God’s truth, opportunities to serve, spiritual gifts, abilities and resources, time and influence, the light or revelation a person has received, etc. Recall that the servant with two talents received THE SAME PRAISE as the servant with five, so the point IS NOT: “Whoever produces the most is the greatest.” Rather, the point is: “Be faithful with what God has given you.” This passage also does not teach salvation by works. The passage does not say that people earn salvation by accumulating good deeds. However, it strongly teaches that a person’s response to God must be real and fruitful, not merely verbal or passive. The third servant calls the master “Lord” in v.24, but he does not faithfully serve him. His words are not matched by obedience. This fits Jesus’ teaching: “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven” (Mt 7:21 KJV) & “Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them” (Mt 7:20 KJV). The faithful servants did not earn the master’s wealth, it belonged to the master from the beginning. They were rewarded because they faithfully used what had been entrusted to them. Respond to the light God gives you, and you will receive more light. Reject or neglect that light, and even the light you have may be lost. Jesus used almost the same statement earlier: “For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath” (Mt 13:12 KJV). However, in this verse, the subject is receiving and responding to spiritual truth. Those who receive God’s truth and respond to it are given greater understanding. Those who reject or neglect the truth lose even the understanding they appeared to possess. 


Matthew 25:30: “and cast ye the unprofitable servant..”: The word “unprofitable” (achreios) means useless, unhelpful, or destitute of utility. He produced zero fruit for the Kingdom. “..into outer darkness..”: This phrase describes the absolute banishment from the presence, light, and warmth of God’s glory into the region of total conscious separation and execution of judgement. “Weeping and gnashing of teeth”: The ultimate expression of conscious torment, inconsolable grief, and bitter, eternal regret. 


*** Faith is never a static concept; authentic faith works by love (Gal 5:6) and produces fruit (Jms 2:17). There are no unassigned believers. God has given every single member of the body of Christ at least “one talent”: whether it is a gift of teaching, giving, prayer, encouragement, or hospitality. Digging a hole in the dirt and hiding it under the guise of humility or fear is an act of treason against the King. God does not judge us merely by what we refrain from doing (like not committing gross external sins); He judges us by what we actively do with the truth, power, and gifts He granted us. Passive neutrality in the Kingdom of God leads straight to the status of the “unprofitable servant.”


Matthew 25:31: “When the Son of man shall come in his glory…”: The title “Son of man” highlights Christ’s true, glorified humanity: the exact human body that was crucified, buried, resurrected and glorified by the Father. He returns not in lowliness or servant-hood, but wrapped in the unveiled divine majesty of God. “...and all the holy angels with him…”: The entirety of the heavenly host accompanies Him as His royal court and executing army (2 Thess 1:7-8). “..then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory”: This is the supreme judicial moment of universe history. The glorified Christ takes His seat as the sole Supreme Judge over all creation. 


*** This verse is one of the most explicit declarations of the Deity of Jesus Christ and the Absolute Unity of God. When Scripture describes the ultimate heavenly throne room, IT NEVER DESCRIBES THREE CHAIRS, THREE DIVINE PERSONS SITTING SIDE-BY-SIDE, OR A COMMITTEE OF DEITIES. There is strictly ONE throne, ONE PERSON occupying that throne, and ONE Name that reveals His identity: (1) ONE Throne in Heaven: Throughout the entire canon of Scripture, the heavenly vision is consistently centered upon a single throne: "I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple” (Isa 6:1 KJV); "And above the firmament... was the likeness of a throne... and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it” (Eze 1:26 KJV); "And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne” (Rev 4:2 KJV). In Rev 4-5, John beholds heaven and repeatedly emphasizes that there is ONE THRONE and ONE WHO SITS UPON IT. There is zero physical or spiritual space for a Trinity of distinct co-equal persons sitting on three individual seats. The divine government of the universe is a monarchy, not a triumvirate. (2) Isaiah saw Jesus on the Throne: Who was the “LORD” (YHWH) that Isaiah saw high and lifted up on that single throne in Isaiah 6? The NT leaves no room for speculation. In John 12:37-41, the Apostle John quotes directly from Isaiah’s throne-room vision (Isa 6:10) and makes an unmistakable declaration: “These things said Esaias [Isaiah], WHEN HE SAW HIS GLORY, AND SPAKE OF HIM [Jesus]” (Jn 12:41 KJV). Under direct Holy Spirit inspiration, John reveals that the glorious God of Israel whom Isaiah saw sitting upon the singular heavenly throne was Jesus, because He is the same YHWH of the OT come in the flesh. Isaiah did not see “God the Father” as a separate person from “God the Son.” He saw the one true God: the eternal Spirit who would eventually manifest Himself in human flesh as Jesus Christ (1 Tim 3:16). (3) ONE Face: By definition, God in His absolute, unapproachable divine essence is an invisible Spirit: “No man hath seen God at any time” (Jn 1:18, 1 Tim 6:16). A pure spirit does not have a physical shape, a human face, or material blood. How, then, does the invisible God reveal Himself visibly to humans and angels? THROUGH THE FACE OF JESUS CHRIST. Jesus is “the image [eikon, visible representation] of the invisible God” (Col 1:15); Jesus is “the express image of His person” (Heb 1:3); God shines in our hearts “to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God IN THE FACE OF JESUS CHRIST” (2 Cor 4:6). When Philip asked Jesus: “Lord, shew us the Father, and it sufficeth us” (Jn 14:8), Jesus did not point to an invisible cloud or a second throne next to Him. He replied: "Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?" (John 14:9 KJV). There is only ONE FACE on the throne of glory because Jesus Christ is the full, complete, and bodily embodiment of the Father: “For in him dwelleth all the fullness of the Godhead bodily” (Col 2:9). When you look at the throne of judgement in Mt 25:31, the face you will see looking back at you is the face of Jesus. (4) ONE Name on the Throne: In ancient Middle Eastern culture, a monarch’s “Name” represented their authority, power, identity, and total character. In Mt 28:19, Jesus commanded His disciples to baptize in the “name” (singular) of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. AS the Apostles understood on the Day of Pentecost (Acts 2:38), “Father,” “Son,” and “Holy Ghost” are non-personal titles describing how the one God manifests Himself to creation: Father in Creation and Fatherhood. Son in Redemption and Incarnation. Holy Ghost in indwelling and Regeneration. The singular NAME that fulfills and encapsulates all those titles (the redemptive, highest name in heaven and earth) is JESUS (YHWH-Savior). As Paul writes in Phil 2:9-11: "Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow... and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father." When Matthew 25:31 states that the Son of Man sits upon the “throne of his glory,” it perfectly matches the ultimate picture of eternity in Revelation 22:3-4: "And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God(invisible Spirit) and of the Lamb(visible human image) shall be in it; and his servants shall serve HIM(not them): And they shall see HIS(one) face; and HIS name(one name) shall be in their foreheads." Notice the singular grammar of Rev 22: There is ONE throne (not two thrones). THey serve HIM (singular pronoun, not them). They shall see HIS face (one face, not multiple faces). HIS name shall be in their foreheads (one singular redemptive name: Jesus). In Mt 23:31, Jesus is not taking a temporary secondary seat. He is sitting as the Almighty God, the Eternal Father (Isa 9:6), and the Glorified Son on the single throne of the universe. He is the Creator, Redeemer, and Judge: the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, and beside Him, there is no other God (Isa 44:6). 


Matthew 25:32: Immediately following the seating of the Son of Man on His singular throne of glory (v. 31), the scene shifts from the coronation of the King to the universal execution of divine judgement. “And before him shall be gathered all nations…”: The scope of this trial is global and exhaustive. The phrase “all nations” (panta ta ethne) encompasses every human being across all ethnic groups, cultures, and political powers throughout history. No world leader, philosopher, or hidden individual escapes this mandatory summons before the throne. “..and he shall separate them one from another..”: This is an active, personal work executed directly by the King. The world today appears mixed: believers and unbelievers live, work, and interact side-by-side in the same cities, workplaces, and families. But human history will not end in a blurred, universal compromise; it ends in an absolute binary division. “..as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats”: In ancient Palestine, sheep and goats regularly grazed together in mixed flocks during the day. However, at dusk, the shepherd had to separate them because goats needed warmth and shelter, whereas sheep could tolerate the cool night air. Furthermore, goats are naturally aggressive, headstrong, and destructive to pasture, while sheep are gentle and obedient to the shepherd’s voice (Jn 10:27). To an untrained observer, Syrian sheep and goats looked similar at a distance, but the shepherd knew the nature of every individual animal in his care. 


Matthew 25:33: “And he shall set the sheep on his right hand…”: In biblical culture and ancient Near Eastern court protocol, the right hand (dexios) is the position of highest honor, authority, favor, safety, and royal inheritance (see Mt 26:64; Acts 2:32-35). The SHEEP represent the righteous, those who surrendered to the Good Shepherd, obeyed the unadulterated Apostolic truth, and allowed their lives to bear the supernatural fruit of the indwelling Spirit. “..but the goats on the left”: The left hand (euonymos) signifies disapproval, rejection, and judgement. The GOATS represent the unrighteous, those who lived in self-will, stubbornness, independence, and rebellion against God’s divine authority. A goat by nature follows its own way, symbolizing human self-righteousness and spiritual lawlessness. 


*** Notice the Spiritual realities of the eternal separation between the sheep and the goats. The Shepherd does not need a lengthy cross-examination or a jury to determine who is a sheep and who is a goat. His judgement is instantaneous because He knows the true nature of every soul. You cannot pretend to be a sheep if you possess the nature of a goat. The King also does not turn sheep into goats or goats into sheep at the throne; He simply separates them baked on what they ALREADY ARE. Our nature is determined in this life through our response to the Gospel: Being born again of water and Spirit (Jn 3:5; Acts 2:38) imparts the nature of Christ (the Lamb/Sheep). Remaining in the unregenerate, self-willed flesh leaves a person with the rebellious nature of the goat. In the throne of Jesus Christ, there is NO MIDDLE GROUP. THere are only two positions: the right hand or the left hand. There is no middle line, no second-chance waiting room, and no third category of “gray area” or “neutrality.” 


Matthew 25:34: “Then shall the King say..”: Jesus officially assumes His supreme title: THE KING. The lowly Nazarene who stood bound before Pontius Pilate now issues unappealable, eternal decrees from the highest throne in the universe. “..unto them on his right hand..”: Addressing the sheep: those who yielded their hearts to Him and bore the fruit of His indwelling Spirit. “Come, ye blessed…”: The initial word of eternity for the believer is an invitation to closer intimacy (“Come”), contrasting sharply with the terrifying decree given to the lost in verse 41 (“Depart from me”). “...of my Father..”: The man Jesus identifies the ultimate source of their covenant blessing: the eternal Spirit, the Father who dwelt within Him (Col 2:9; 2 Cor 5:19; Jn 14:9). “..inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world”: Salvation is not an afterthought or a last-minute reaction to human sin. Before the cosmos was formed, God’s sovereign plan ordained a kingdom for His redeemed people. 


*** Who is “The King”? Who is sitting on the throne and speaking as “The King”? Trinitarian theology often attempts to divine the judgement scene by placing “God the Father” on the throne while “God the Son” stands alongside Him on His “right hand” as an advocate or mediator. However, it is “the Son of man” who sits upon the singular throne of glory. Therefore, Jesus Christ himself is “The King” who speaks in v.34. When Jesus refers to “my Father” he is not sitting on a throne next to a distinct second divine person called “the Father.” Rather, the VISIBLE KING sitting on the throne is the Son (God manifest in real human flesh, 1 Tim 3:16), and the Father is the eternal, invisible Spirit dwelling within that glorified human body (Jn 14:10; Col 2:9).


*** Why does Jesus say “Blessed of My Father”? Trinitarian critics often point to phrases like “my Father” to argue for a distinction of divine persons within the Godhead. However, the distinction is not between divine persons, but between humanity and divinity: (1) According to His humanity (The Son): As a real, authentic man, Jesus possesses a genuine human relationship with God. When God took on flesh, He entered into our physical realm by indwelling a real human person. In this realm, humans run off the Spirit of God, without the Spirit of God, no one would have life. Jesus, being a man, is also subject to the rules of men: he runs off the Spirit of God. The only difference being that the man Jesus was the only sinless man and that he was full of the Holy Spirit (Lk 4:1), and had access to this divine Spirit “without limit” (Jn 3:34 BSB). This human has a temporary role of mediator, but at the end of the age, he, too, will submit to the divine Spirit and end this mediator role: “And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all” (1 Cor 15:28 KJV). (2) According to His Deity (The Father): The eternal Spirit inside Jesus is the Father YHWH. Isaiah 9:6 explicitly prophesied that the Son born to us would be called “The everlasting Father,” and recall that we only have ONE Father (Mal 2:10). So when Jesus says: “Come, ye blessed of my Father,” he speaks as the Glorified God-Man. His human mouth articulates the judgement, acknowledging that the eternal plan of redemption and the divine kingdom were conceived by the infinite, indwelling Spirit: the Father. Jesus is not deferring to a separate deity in another chair; he is revealing that the blessings administered through his human hands originated from the eternal Spirit of God that resided within him. We see this duality active in Rev 22:3-4, where the ONE throne has God & the Lamb under one face and under one name. The Father is God in His transcendent, invisible relation to creation (the Originator of the Kingdom “from the foundation of the world”). The Son is God in His incarnate, visible relation to humanity (the King executing judgement in a visible body). Jesus uses “my Father” because the inheritance being handed down to the sheep was established in eternity past by the invisible God BEFORE THE INCARNATION took place in time. The King on the throne is the visible embodiment of that exact same invisible Father!


*** How do believers become those “blessed of my Father” who inherit the kingdom? Paul explains the exact legal mechanism: “For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received THE SPIRIT OF ADOPTION, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together” (Rom 8:15-17 KJV) & “And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ” (Gal 4:6-7 KJV). To inherit the kingdom prepared by the Father, a person must be adopted into the family of God: “But ye are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if so be that the Spirit of God dwell in you. Now if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his” (Rom 8:9 KJV). According to the Apostolic blueprint of Acts 2:38, when a person repents, is baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, and receives the infilling of the Holy Spirit, they receive the very Spirit of the Father promised by the prophet Joel (Acts 2:16-17). It is the indwelling Holy Spirit, the oil in the vessel (Mt 25:4), that marks a believer as a child of the Father, qualifying them to stand at the King’s right hand in Mt 25:34 and hear the glorious decree: “Inherit the kingdom prepared for you!” Recall that Jesus said: “by their fruits ye shall know them” (Mt 7:20 KJV), so if you show the “fruits of the Spirit,” that’s a good sign that you abiding in Jesus and therefore are saved: “the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Gal 5:22-23 KJV). 


Matthew 25:35: Having welcomed the righteous to inherit the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world (v.34), the King now presents the evidence for his verdict. He does not cite their theological knowledge, public status, or church office, but rather the practical, sacrificial fruit produced by their faith. “For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat”: The word “meat” in the KJV simply means “food” or “nourishment” (broma in Greek). The King identifies directly with the physical suffering of the needy. Authentic, Spirit-filled faith is never purely abstract or intellectual; it responds directly to basic human deprivation. “...I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink”: Providing water to a thirsty soul represents the simplest, most fundamental act of mercy. Jesus previously noted that a cup of cold water given to one of his disciples would be specially rewarded (Mt 10:41-42). “...I was a stranger, and ye took me in”: “Stranger” (xenos) refers to an outsider, traveler, or foreigner. Hospitably opening one’s home and fellowship to an outsider required vulnerability, trust, and sacrificial love.
