The other parallel passage, John 19:25, identifies this Mary as “Mary the WIFE OF CLOPAS.” Hegesippus (a 2nd-century Christian historian whose writings are preserved by Eusebius of Caesarea in Ecclesiastical History, Book III, Ch. 11) explicitly states that Clopas was the brother of Joseph (Jesus' earthly foster father). This makes Mary of Clopas the sister-in-law of Mary the mother of Jesus. Her sons (JAMES THE LESS, JOSES, and SIMEON) were Jesus' legal cousins, not His uterine half-brothers. So we have three JAMES: (1) JAMES THE JUST, son of Mary, the half-brother of Jesus (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3). He is specifically called “the Lord’s brother” in order to differentiate him from the other James (Gal 1:19). This James initially DID NOT believe in Jesus (Jn 7:5). But James apparently became a believer AFTER Jesus’ resurrection (1 Cor 15:7). This James eventually became a major leader in the Jerusalem church. In Acts 15, James speaks authoritatively during the Jerusalem council, even with Peter present: “Wherefore MY SENTENCE IS…” (Acts 15:19 KJV). Paul later says: “James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars…” (Gal 2:9 KJV). And Acts 21:18 says that Paul would go to the elders of the Jerusalem Church: “Paul went in with us UNTO JAMES; and all the elders were present”; (2) JAMES THE GREATER, son of Zebedee (Mt 4:21), and one of the apostles (Mt 4:21). James the son of Zebedee was particularly prominent among the Twelve. Mark states Jesus called him and his brother John “Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder” (Mk 3:17 KJV). He was often part of the inner circle of Jesus. Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him for several major events. For example, the raising of Jairus’ daughter (Mk 5:37), the Transfiguration (Mt 17:1), and Gethsemane (Mk 14:33). This James was also the FIRST OF THE TWELVE TO BE MARTYRED (Acts 12:2 KJV). This is James SON OF ZEBEDEE, not James THE LORD’S BROTHER or James SON OF ALPHAEUS/CLOPAS. (3) JAMES THE LESS: This is James the son of Alphaeus (Mt 10:3; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15). He is another one of the twelve apostles. He is called “THE LESS” because he is traditionally linked to James “THE LESS” in Mark 15:40, son of “the other Mary.” This “other Mary” is the “wife of Cleophas” (Jn 19:25; Mt 27:56; Mk 15:40). If the husband’s name is “Cleophas,” then James THE LESS’ father is Cleophas. But since he was listed as “James the SON OF ALPHAEUS,” many people make the assumption that Cleophas and Alphaeus are the same person. Either the father of James THE LESS has two names, or there are multiple translations of the Hebrew name into Greek. The Greek names are: Κλωπᾶς (Clopas) and Ἀλφαῖος (Alphaeus). There are historical/linguistic reasons why some have proposed that these represent different forms of the same underlying Hebrew name, however, the NT is never explicit about it. But we cannot discard completely the possibility of 4 James, rather than 3: (1) James the Greater (Son of Zebedee and brother of John); (2) James the Lord’s brother and leader of the Jerusalem Church; (3) James the son of Alphaeus, which was one of the twelve disciples; (4) James the Less, someone with no prominence whatsoever in the NT. 


Matthew 27:56: “Among which was Mary Magdalene..”: Mary from the town of Magdala. She is consistently named first in the Gospel lists of women, signifying her leadership and prominent role as a witness. Jesus had cast seven demons out of her (Lk 8:2), and her deep devotion kept her at the cross and brought her first to the empty tomb on East morning. “...and Mary the mother of James and Joses..”: A key female disciple identified by her sons to distinguish her from Mary the mother of Jesus, and Mary Magdalene. As demonstrated across the parallel accounts, this is Mary of Clopas (early church tradition, Hegesippus, says she is the sister-in-law of Joseph and aunt of Jesus), and her son is James the Less (Mk 15:40), one of the Twelve Apostles. “..and the mother of Zebedee’s children”: The mother of the apostles James (the Greater who was the first to be martyred) and John, the beloved disciple (Mt 10:2). In Mt 20:20-23, she approached Jesus asking for her two sons to sit at his right and left hands in his kingdom. Cross-referencing Mk 15:40 reveals her proper name: Salome. John’s parallel account shows: (1) Jesus’ “mother, and (2) his mother’s sister, (3) Mary the wife of Cleophas, and (4) Mary Magdalene” (Jn 19:25 KJV). Since we know for sure who Jesus’ mother & Mary Magdalene are, the most probable harmonization of the gospels is that (3) “Mary the wife of Cleophas” is the mother of James and Joses(v.56), and “Salome” is (2) the sister of Mary the mother of Jesus. This means that James the Greater and John (the beloved disciple) are Jesus’ first cousins. 


*** The women described at the cross by the different Gospel authors: 
(1) Matthew 27:55-56: (a) Mary Magdalene; (b) Mary the mother of James and Joses; (c) The mother of Zebedee’s children. 
(2) Mark 15:40-41: (a) Mary Magdalene; (b) Mary the mother of James the less and Joses; (c) Salome.
(3) Luke 23:49, 24:10: (a) Mary Magdalene; (b) Mary the mother of James; (c) Joanna; (d) “Other women that were with them” / “Women that followed him from Galilee”
(4) John 19:25: (a) His mother [Mary, mother of Jesus]; (b) His mother’s sister; (c) Mary the wife of Clopas (Cleophas); (d) Mary Magdalene.


Matthew 27:57: “When the even was come…”: Jewish law mandated that executed criminals could not remain hanging on a tree overnight (Deut 21:22-23). Furthermore, because the Sabbath began at sunset (around 6:00 PM), the burial had to occur swiftly before the holy day commenced. “..there came a rich man of Arimathea, named Joseph…”: Arimathea was a Jewish town (likely the OT Ramathaim-zophim, birthplace of Samuel). Mark 15:43 adds that Joseph was an honorable member of the Sanhedrin, though Luke 23:51 clarifies he had not consented to their vote against Jesus. “..who also himself was Jesus’ disciple”: John 19:38 notes he was a disciple “secretly for fear of the Jews.” Jesus’ death acted as the catalyst that forced Joseph out of hiding to take a public stand for his Master.


Matthew 27:58: “He went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus”: Standard Roman practice for executed rebels (perduellio) was to leave their bodies on the cross to rot or throw them into a common grave for criminals. It took immense courage for Joseph to approach the Roman Governor Pontius Pilate. Requesting the body aligned Joseph directly with a man condemned for treason against Rome, threatening his wealth, status, and seat on the Sanhedrin. “Then Pilate commanded the body to be delivered”: Mark 15:44-45 records that Pilate was surprised Jesus was already dead and confirmed it with the centurion before releasing the body to Joseph. 


Matthew 27:59: “And when Joseph had taken the body..”: Cross-referencing John 19:39, Joseph was joined by Nicodemus (another secret disciple on the Sanhedrin), who brought roughly 100 pounds of myrrh and aloes to prepare the body. “...he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth”: “Linen cloth” (sindōn) was fine, expensive linen sheet. Wrapping the body with burial spices was the customary Jewish preparation for honorable burial, ensuring the body was handled with reverence rather than cast into a mass grave.


Matthew 27:60: “And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock..”: John 19:41 specifies that no one had ever been laid in this “new tomb” before. This detail rules out any claims that Jesus’ eventual resurrection was confused with another corpse in the tomb. This fulfills Isaiah 53:9 written over 700 years earlier: “And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death.” Jesus died among criminals, but was buried in a wealthy ruler’s tomb. “...and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed”: Rock-hewn tombs were secured by a large, heavy stone(golel) rolled along a slanted groove to block the entrance from tomb robbers and animals. Joseph’s tomb provided an exact, known location for both the Roman guards (vv 62-66) and the Galilean women to monitor, ensuring there was no confusion about which tomb was found empty on Easter morning. Jesus literally died. He did not merely faint or swoon on the cross; he died and was formally prepared for burial by two high-ranking Jewish leaders. 


Matthew 27:61: “And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary…”: As established earlier (Mt 27:56, Jn 19:25), the “other Mary” was Mary of Clopas, mother of James the Less and Joses. “...sitting over against the sepulchre”: While Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus prepared and sealed the tomb, these women sat directly opposite the entrance. They took careful mental note of the precise physical location where Jesus was placed (Mk 15:47) so they could return after the Sabbath with additional spices (Lk 23:56).


Matthew 27:62: “Now the next day, that followed the day of the preparation..”: The “day of preparation” was Friday (the day before the Sabbath, when Passover preparations took place). “The next day” means Saturday, the Jewish Sabbath. “..the chief priests and Pharisees came together unto Pilate”: the religious leaders were so consumed by fear that they broke their own strict Sabbath regulations to conduct business with a pagan ROman governor, securing a legal order on a holy day.


Matthew 27:63: “Saying, Sir, we remember that that deceiver said..”: They contemptuously label Jesus a “deceiver” (planot- a fraud or imposter). “...while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again”: ironically, Christ’s enemies understood his predictions of resurrection (Mt 12:40; 16:21; 20:19) far more clearly at this moment than his own scattered disciples did. They took his words seriously enough to guard against any potential fulfillment. 


Matthew 27:64: “Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day…”: they demand Roman authorization to secure the tomb through the three-day window to prevent any fraudulent claims. “...lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away…”: they anticipated a staged resurrection, worrying the disciples would spirit the body away and proclaim him risen. “...so the last error shall be worse than the first”: the “first error” was people believing Jesus was the promised Messiah during his living ministry. The “last error” is people believing he rose from the dead. They recognized that a risen Messiah would ignite an unstoppable movement far greater than his earthly ministry. 


Matthew 27:65: “Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch…”: the phrase (echete koustōdian) can mean either “Take a Roman guard” or “Use your existing Temple guard.” The BSB translates it as: “You have a guard… Go, make the tomb as secure as you know how.” Most scholars agree Pilate assigned a Roman guard unit (koustōdia), consisting of 4 to 16 heavily armed Roman soldiers. “..go your way, make it as sure as ye can’: Pilate gives them full authority to use whatever security measures they deem necessary to make the tomb completely unbreachable.


Matthew 27:66: “So they went, and made the sepulchre sure…”: the Jewish leaders took full advantage of Pilate’s decree to secure the tomb via two distinct Roman mechanisms: (1) “sealing the stone” (sphragisantes): a string or cord was stretched across the large rolling stone and anchored on both sides of the rock face with soft clay or wax, stamped with the official imperial seal of Rome. Breaking this seal carried the immediate death penalty under Roman law. (2) “setting a watch”: stationing the Roman guard around the tomb to keep vigil day and night. By placing hostile Roman guards at the tomb, the Sanhedrin inadvertently provided unbiased, non-Christian witnesses who would later report the supernatural earthquake and the angel on Sunday morning (Mt 28:11-15). The combination of a massive stone, an unbroken Roman seal, and a detachment of Roman soldiers completely destroyed any argument that the disciples could have slipped past, broken in, and stolen the corpse.
Matthew 28
Matthew 28:1: “In the end of the sabbath..”: The Jewish Sabbath ran from sunset Friday evening to sunset Saturday evening. The phrase “in the end of the sabbath” means after the Sabbath had fully ended and passed: specifically early Sunday morning. “...as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week..”: The Greek term “epiphosko” (“began to dawn”) signifies the transition of daylight broken across the horizon on Sunday morning. This marks the dawn of a new covenant era: the Lords’ Day. “...came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary..”: Mary Magdalene, the one out of whom Jesus had cast seven devils out (Mk 16:9). “The other Mary” is identified in Matthew 27:56 as Mary the mother of James and Joses (the wife of Cleopas/Clopas). “..to see the sepulchre”: Matthew notes their original intent: they came to inspect the tomb, expecting to find the corpse of Jesus intact behind the sealed stone. 


*** Atheists and muslims often cite these verses to attack the Bible, so we will harmonize them as we go. First, what was the time of arrival? Matthew 28:1: “As it began to dawn toward the first day of the week..”; Mark 16:2: “Very early in the morning… at the rising of the sun;” Luke 24:1: “Very early in the morning..”; John 20:1: “Early, when it was yet dark…” - all these descriptions reflect the natural progression of twilight to sunrise. The women gathered, purchased/prepared spices, and left their lodging while it was still dark (Jn 20:1). As they walked across Jerusalem/Bethany toward the tomb, twilight broke (“began to dawn” - Matthew/Luke), and by the time they actually reached the sepulcher outside the walls, the sun had begun rising (“at the rising of the sun” - Mark). What about the women? Matthew 28:1: Names Mary Magdalene and “the other Mary.” Mark 16:1: Names Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. Luke 24:10: Names Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and “other women that were with them.” And John 20:1: Mentions Mary Magdalene individually. - notice there is no contradiction at all. No writer states that ONLY the women he listed were present. John focuses exclusively on Mary Magdalene’s personal journey because of her pivotal private interaction with the resurrected Lord in the garden (Jn 20:11-18). Yet, even in John’s account, Mary uses the plural pronoun when she runs to Peter: “WE know not where they have laid him” (Jn 20:2), proving she was in a group. Matthew and Mark highlight the primary leaders among the women (the two Marys and Salome, the mother of James and John). Luke provides the comprehensive list, explicitly adding Joanna (the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward; Luke 8:3) and a larger group of female disciples. 


** While the male apostles were hiding behind locked doors out of fear of the Jews (Jn 20:19), these faithful women were the last at the cross on Friday and the first at the tomb on Sunday. If the Gospel writers had conspired to invent a fraudulent resurrection story, they would have their details identical, and under 1st-century Jewish legal culture, they would have fabricated MALE witnesses, and the witness of women was disregarded. The natural variations in their accounts and their reliance on female testimony validate the genuine historical truth of the Gospel records. 


Matthew 28:2: “And, behold, there was a great earthquake..”: A divine manifestation (theophany). Just as an earthquake marked the moment of Christ’s death on the cross (Mt 27:51), another earthquake signals his cosmic victory over death at his resurrection. “...for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven…”: God dispatched a heavenly messenger to intervene directly at the sealed tomb. “...and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it”: The stone was not rolled away to let Jesus OUT; as a resurrected, glorified body, He was no longer bound by physical walls (Jn 20:19). Rather, the stone was rolled away to let the witnesses IN to verify that the tomb was already empty. The angel sitting on top of the massive stone was a posture of supreme triumph over Roman authority, imperial seals, and hte power of death. 


Matthew 28:3: “His countenance was like lightning…”: His face radiated the dazzling, unapproachable glory of God’s presence (like Mt 17:2 at the Transfiguration). “...and his raiment white as snow”: His clothing reflected absolute heavenly purity and holiness, contrasting sharply with the darkness of the tomb and the corruption of human plotters. 


Matthew 28:4: “And for fear of him the keepers did shake…”: The “keepers” were the Roman guard detail sent by Pilate to secure the tomb (Mt 27:62-66). Hardened Roman soldiers, trained in war and terror, were overcome with intense panic (epseisthesan - they quaked like the earthquake itself). “...and became as dead men”: They collapsed into a state of paralyzed, unconscious shock. Ironically, while the dead Savior became alive, the living soldiers became like dead men. 


Matthew 28: 5: “And the angel answered and said unto the women…”: Addressing the terrified women who had now reached the entrance, the angel gently speaks peace to them. “Fear not ye…”: The pronoun “ye” is emphatic in Greek (“You do not fear”). The pagan guards had every reason to tremble in judgement, but faithful disciples who love Jesus have no reason to fear heavenly messengers. “...for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified”: The angel explicitly acknowledges their devotion to the crucified Lord. 


Matthew 28:6: “He is not here: for he is risen…’: The central proclamation of Christianity. The resurrection is presented not as a mystical metaphor, but as a bodily, historical fact. “...as he said”: The angel reminds them that Jesus had repeatedly prophesied his own death and third-day resurrection (Mt 16:21; 17:22-23; 20:19). God’s Word was proven completely trustworthy. “Come, see the place where the Lord lay”: The angel invites them inside the burial chamber to inspect the empty stone slab and verify the evidence for themselves. 


Matthew 28:7: “And go quickly, and tell his disciples…”: The women are commissioned as the first witnesses and messengers (apostles to the apostles) of the resurrection. “..he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him..”: Reaffirming Jesus’ prior promise at the Last Supper (Mt 26:32), the main corporate meeting between the resurrected King and his scattered flock would take place in Galilee (Mt 28:16-20). 


Matthew 28:8: “And they departed quickly from the sepulchre..”: They immediately obeyed the angel’s command without hesitation. “...with fear and great joy..’: A holy mixture of emotions: fear (reverent awe in the presence of the supernatural) and great joy (overwhelming gladness that their Master was alive). “...and did run to bring his disciples word”: Urgency filled their feet as they ran across Jerusalem to report the empty tomb. 


*** Harmonizing the Gospels: (1) Did the women see the earthquake and Angel descend? (Mt 28:2 vs Mk/Lk/Jn): Matthew 28:2-4 does a Parenthetical/Flashback to provide background context (“Now there had been a great earthquake…”) explaining HOW the tomb was opened before the women got there. When the women actually stepped into the garden, the guards had already collapsed/fled, and the stone was already rolled back (Mk 16:4; Lk 24:2; Jn 20:1). (2) One Angel or Two Angels?: Matthew 28:2,5 & Mark 16:5 Mention ONE Angel addressing the women. Luke 24:4 & John 20:12 mention TWO Angels in dazzling apparel. Resolution: Matthew and Mark focus on the single angle WHO SPOKE as the spokesman for the heavenly pair. Mentioning one spokesman does not deny the presence of a second angel (where there are two, there is always one). (3) Outside or Inside the Tomb?: Matthew 28:2,6 shows the angel sitting on the rolled-back stone outside, then inviting them: “Come, see the place where the Lord lay” (v.6), leading them inside. Mark 16:5 & Luke 24:3-4 show the women stepping inside the tomb chamber, where they see the angels sitting/standing near the burial slab. Resolution: The angel who rolled away the stone sat upon it INITIALLY OUTSIDE, spoke reassurance to the approaching women (v.5), and escorted/guided them INSIDE the tomb vault to show them the folded grave clothes (v.6).


*** The Stone was rolled away for us. Jesus did not need an open tomb to exit, but we needed an open tomb to see that he was gone. The empty grave stands as physical proof of justification (“Who was delivered for our offences, and was raised again for our justification,” Rom 4:25 KJV). 


*** The first witnesses of the New Creation were women. God bypassed the Sanhedrin, Pilate, and the high priests, entrusting the greatest news in human history to humble, devoted women: reversing the curse of Eden and elevating the weak things of the world to confound the mighty (1 Cor 1:27).


Matthew 28:9: “And as they went to tell his disciples…”: Their obedience to the angel’s instruction (v.7) put them directly in the path of blessing. As they ran to deliver the message to the apostles, Christ revealed himself to them. “..behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail”: The greeting “All hail” translates the common Greek greeting “Chairete,” which literally means “Rejoice!” or “Peace be unto you!” It was a warm, joyful, everyday greeting transformed into a glorious resurrection reality. “...And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him”: Holding him by the feet was a physical gesture of total submission, reverence, and desperate affection. It also proved the BODILY resurrection of Jesus Christ. He was not a phantom, spirit, or hallucination, but possessed tangible flesh and bones (“Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have,” Lk 24:39). By accepting their worship (proskuneo), Jesus affirmed His absolute deity. Under strict Jewish law, worship belonged exclusively to God (ex 20:3-5; Mt 4:10). 


Matthew 28:10: “Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid…”: Just as the angel said in verse 5, Jesus calms their lingering shock and overwhelming awe. “...go tell my brethren..”: THIS IS THE FIRST TIME Jesus refers to his disciples as his “brethren” (adelphoi). Despite their recent abandonment, cowardice, and Peter’s denials during his trial, Jesus does not call them “traitors” or “deserters”: he calls them his brothers. His resurrection established a new covenant relationship where believers are sons of God and joint-heirs with Christ (“The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together,” Rom 8:16-17 KJV). “..that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me”: Jesus reconfirms the appointed rendezvous location in Galilee, away from the immediate hostility of Jerusalem, where he would deliver the Great Commission (vv. 16-20). 


Matthew 28:11: “Now when they were going…”: Matthew sets up a dramatic parallel: while the women are running with joy to tell the disciples, the Roman guards are running in terror to report to the priests. “...some of the watch came into the city…”: The “watch” was the Roman guard detail assigned to seal and secure the tomb (Mt 27:62-66). “...and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done”: The soldiers knew that reporting a failed mission and a missing body to their Roman superiors meant automatic execution under Roman military law. Therefore, they fled to the Jewish chief priests (their original employers for this specific assignment) hoping for protection and a way to explain the supernatural earthquake and missing body. 


Matthew 28:12: “And when they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel…”: The Sanhedrin held an emergency morning session. Instead of repenting when confronted with undeniable evidence of the Resurrection, their hardened hearts immediately sought a way to suppress the truth. “...they gave large money unto the soldiers”: They offered a substantial bribe (arguria hikanas: “a significant sum of silver”). Just as thirty pieces of silver were used to betray Jesus in their hands (Mt 26:15), silver was once again used to manufacture a lie about his resurrection.


Matthew 28:13: "Saying, Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away..." The official conspiracy fabricated by the Sanhedrin to explain the empty tomb. The Absurdity of the Fabricated lie: (1) If the soldiers were genuinely asleep, how could they possibly know or testify that it was the disciples who stole the body? Witnesses cannot testify about events that occurred while they were unconscious! (2) Sleeping on watch was a capital crime in the Roman army punishable by death. No trained Roman soldier would voluntarily admit to sleeping on duty unless guaranteed absolute immunity and political protection. (3) The disciples were cowering in fear behind locked doors (Jn 20:19). It is historically improbable that fearful, unarmed fishermen could quietly roll away a multi-ton stone and overpower or bypass a squad of armed Roman guards without waking a single one. J


Matthew 28:14: “And if this come to the governor’s ears…”: If news reached Pontius Pilate that the guards fell asleep on duty, standard discipline required their execution. "...we will persuade him, and secure you." The chief priests promised to use their political influence, bribes, and leverage over Pilate (the same pressure they used to secure Jesus' crucifixion) to ensure the soldiers suffered no military penalties.


Matthew 28:15: "So they took the money, and did as they were taught..." The guards took the bribe and spread the manufactured narrative. "...and this saying is commonly reported among the Jews until this day." At the time Matthew wrote his Gospel (decades after the Resurrection), the "stolen body" theory remained the primary anti-Christian polemic used by the Jewish religious leadership to counter the Christian proclamation of the Risen Christ.


*** By manufacturing the "stolen body" story, the enemies of Christ inadvertently conceded the foundational historical fact of Christianity: the tomb was undeniably empty. If the body had remained in the grave, the Sanhedrin could have easily crushed the early church simply by producing the corpse.


*** Jesus' message to "tell my brethren" demonstrates that His grace and love toward His followers are anchored in His completed work, not their perfection. He restored them from cowardice into bold witnesses who would ultimately lay down their lives preaching the Resurrection.


Matthew 28:16: "Then the eleven disciples went away into Galilee..." Obedient to the angel’s message (Mt 28:7) and Jesus’ direct command (Mt 28:10), the disciples gathered at the designated mountain.


Matthew 28:17: "...they worshipped him: but some doubted." The disciples offered divine worship (proskuneo) to the risen Christ. Worshipping Jesus is appropriate because He is not merely a second divine Person alongside God, but God Himself manifested in flesh (1 Tim 3:16). The lingering hesitation ("some doubted") highlights their initial struggle to grasp the physical reality of His resurrection.


Matthew 28:18: “All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth”: If “all power” in both heaven and earth is given to Jesus, he cannot be a “co-equal, co-eternal second person” who lacked power UNTIL it was delegated to him, rather it reveals the absolute deity of Jesus Christ. God is strictly one single divine Spirit (YHWH) who manifested Himself fully in human flesh as Jesus Christ (2 Cor 5:19; Col 2:9). Because God as pure Spirit possesses all inherent, uncreated authority, the statement that authority was “given” does not describe one divine person handing power to a distinct second divine person within a Trinity. Rather, it describes the dynamics of the Incarnation: the infinite, eternal divine Spirit (YHWH) fully investing and exalting the genuine human flesh (the Son) so that the divine and the human are indivisibly united in one visible God. The authentic sinless human born of Mary, was brought into total, exalted union with the indwelling deity of YHWH, creating a seamless fusion of divinity and humanity (Jn 10:30) where the human Messiah acts with the absolute, unlimited power of God Almighty Himself, positioned in the “right hand of power’ (Mt 26:64). Since the OT explicitly declares that ultimate cosmic authority, glory, and salvation belong exclusively to YHWH (“power belongeth unto God,” Ps 62:11; “I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another..”, Isa 42:8; “..I am God, and there is none else…That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear,” Isa 45:22-23; “I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God,” Isa 44:6), the declaration that Jesus possesses ALL AUTHORITY in heaven and on earth proves that he is not merely a representative or a second persona, but YHWH Himself revealed in human flesh. If Jesus holds all power in both realms, there is no remaining divine authority left outside of him: “ye are COMPLETE in him” (Col 2:10 KJV). Consequently, when Jesus transitions immediately from declaring his supreme authority in v.18 to commanding the Great Commission in vv. 19-20, his instruction to baptize must reflect that singular, supreme authority. It would be entirely illogical for Jesus to proclaim that all power and authority belong to him, only to command his followers to go and baptize in the names of other distinct persons or titles separate from himself. Instead, because the singular “name” of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost is the exalted, saving name of “Jesus” (the name that embodies the full presence and authority of YHWH as “YHWH-saves”) the disciples correctly understood his command. Thus, when they went out to fulfill the Great Commission throughout the Book of Acts, they consistently baptized strictly in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 2:38; 8:12; 8:16; 10:48; 19:5; 22:16), recognizing that the one who spoke to them in Mt 28:18 was indeed the ONE God manifest in the flesh, not just a member of some Trinity of divine persons.




Matthew 28:19: “..baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost..”: The word “name” (onoma) is SINGULAR, not plural (“names”). Jesus did not command baptism into the “names” of three distinct persons, but into the one singular Name that encompasses Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. “Father,” “Son,” and “Holy Ghost” are titles, roles, or manifestations of the one God, not proper names. Father describes God’s relationship as Creator, Originator, and Father of the human Jesus. Son describes the human born of Mary in whom the one God fully dwelt and was manifested in the flesh for human redemption (the deity clothed in humanity). The Holy Ghost describes God’s Spirit in active, invisible relation to believers and creation. All three titles are ascribed to Jesus in Isaiah 9:6: “For unto us a child is born, unto us a (1)SON is given... and his name shall be called .. (2) COUNSELLOR(the Spirit), The mighty God, The everlasting (3) FATHER ..” (Isa 9:6 KJV) - and recall we only have ONE FATHER (Mal 2:10). The Bible is very clear that the name is always “JESUS” (YHWH-saves): (1) The NAME of the Son: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mt 1:21 KJV) - not even a Trinitarian would argue that the name of the Son is “JESUS.” However, for a Trinitarian, “JESUS” IS NOT the name ABOVE every name, for them “Lord” is the name above every name. For them “JESUS” is simply the human name that the second person of the Trinity used while on Earth. John MacArthur, a popular Trinitarian Baptist pastor, writes: “Christ’s new name which further describes His essential nature and places Him above and beyond all comparison is ‘Lord’” (Phil 2:9 MacArthur Study Bible Study Notes). A Oneness does not have to fight Scripture on this, for we know “JESUS”(YHWH-Saves) is the NAME ABOVE EVERY NAME: “Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and GIVEN HIM A NAME WHICH IS ABOVE EVERY NAME: That at the name of JESUS every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth” (Phil 2:9-10 KJV). (2) The NAME of the Father: The Father in the OT went by the name: YHWH (“I am the LORD[YHWH]... but by my name JEHOVAH[YHWH] was I not known to them,” Ex 6:2-3 KJV). He always used a name that matched what He was doing. For example: YHWH-yir’eh (“YHWH will provide,” Gen 22:14), YHWH-rof’ekha (“YHWH your healer,” Ex 15:26), YHWH-nissî (“YHWH is my banner,” Ex 17:15), YHWH-shālôm (“YHWH is peace”, Judges 6:24), etc. but now, in the NT, He has decided to go by the name “YHWH-saves” or “YHWH-savior.” The name of “JESUS” comes from the Hebrew/Aramaic Jewish name “Yeshua”, a shorter form of “Yehoshua” - the same name as “Joshua,” the man who brought the Israelites into the promised land, a shadow of what Jesus would later do (the LXX translated the book of “Joshua” as “Iesous,” the same Greek word used for “Jesus;” and the KJV translators translated “Iesous” as “Jesus” in Heb 4:8, even though the context is talking about “Joshua” from the OT). “Yeho-” is a shortened form of the divine name “YHWH”, while “-shua” refers to the Hebrew root “yāsha”, which means to “save”, “deliver”, or “salvation”: this is why the man Jesus HAD to be named “JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins” (Mt 1:21 KJV). Mary did not randomly choose the name “JESUS,” she was instructed by the angel to specifically name him “JESUS” (Mt 1:21). The human born of Mary INHERITED THE NAME from the Father (Heb 1:4), the NAME ABOVE EVERY NAME (Phil 2:9). The name of the Father was placed on the human, the same way the name of YHWH was placed on the Temple in the OT (“In this house, and in Jerusalem … will I put MY NAME for ever”, 2 Kings 21:7 KJV). Having the NAME of God means that God is present, for we know God was literally present at the Temple (“the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD,” 1 Kings 8:10-11 KJV). In the NT, the human Jesus is the new temple of the divine Spirit (In Jn 2:19, Jesus says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”) because “God was IN Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself” (2 Cor 5:19 KJV). The name came from the Father, that’s why Jesus could say: “I will declare THY NAME unto my brethren” (Heb 2:12 KJV), and “I am come in my FATHER’s NAME” (Jn 5:43 KJV), and “the works that I do in my FATHER’S NAME, they bear witness of me” (Jn 10:25 KJV), and “I have manifested THY NAME unto the men..” (Jn 17:6 KJV) and “Holy Father, protect them BY YOUR NAME, THE NAME YOU GAVE ME” (Jn 17:11 BSB; the CT and MT read like this, the TR decided to follow the Latin in this specific verse, perhaps they, being Trinitarian, felt nervous writing that the Father had given His name to the Son) and “I protected and preserved them BY YOUR NAME, THE NAME YOU GAVE ME” (Jn 17:12 BSB), and “I have declared unto them THY NAME” (Jn 17:26 KJV) - and of course Jesus manifested, declared, and preached the name of “JESUS.” In Revelation, the apostle John also writes that he “saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion, and with Him 144,000 who had HIS NAME and HIS FATHER’s NAME written on their foreheads” (Rev 14:1 BSB), likewise, both God and the lamb are presented as one being with one face and one singular NAME: “The throne of God(Spirit) and of the Lamb(flesh) will be within the city, and HIS(singular masculine) servants will worship HIM(singular masculine). They will see HIS(singular masculine) face(just one face), and HIS NAME(singular name) will be on their foreheads” (Rev 22:3-4 BSB). Hence, since the Son inherited and came in the name of the Father, then the name of the Father must also be: “YHWH-Saves” (Jesus). (3) The NAME of the HOLY SPIRIT: Since the Holy Spirit is the same thing as the Father, of course His name will also be “YHWH-saves” (Jesus). The Father is a Spirit (Jn 4:24) and the Father is “Holy” (Jn 17:11), hence “Holy Spirit,” that’s why it was the Holy Spirit that literally CONCEIVED(begot) baby Jesus in Mary’s womb (Mt 1:20), making the Holy Spirit the literal Father of the Son. But if you need more Scriptural support, here it is: “...the HOLY SPIRIT prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia … the SPIRIT OF JESUS would not permit them” (Acts 16:6-7 BSB) - in the CT, it more clearly identifies the “HOLY SPIRIT” with the “SPIRIT OF JESUS,” using them interchangeably. Also: “But ye are not in the flesh, but in the SPIRIT, if so be that the SPIRIT OF GOD dwell in you. Now if any man have not the SPIRIT OF CHRIST, he is none of his” (Rom 8:9 KJV) - recall there is ONLY ONE SPIRIT (Eph 4:4), and Paul says it’s the “SPIRIT OF CHRIST.” Which Spirit worked in the prophets of the OT? Peter says it was the “HOLY SPIRIT” in 2 Peter 1:20-21, but then says it was the “SPIRIT OF CHRIST” in 1 Peter 1:10-11, again, using the two titles interchangeably. Then look at John 14:16-18: “And I(human Jesus) will pray the Father(divine Spirit), and He(the Father) shall give you another Comforter(instead of the man Jesus full of the Holy Spirit, the new Comforter will be the invisible Spirit working IN us), that he may abide with you for ever(as Spirit); Even the SPIRIT OF TRUTH(Holy Spirit); whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not(it’s invisible), neither knoweth him: but ye know him(since it dwells in the man Jesus & they’ve met Jesus); for He dwelleth with you(infilling the man Jesus), and shall be IN you(no longer within the man Jesus, but withIN every believer). I(Jesus) will not leave you comfortless(or “as orphans,” BSB, aka WITHOUT A FATHER): I(Jesus) will come to you(as Spirit)” (KJV) - Jesus fulfilling the duties of the entire Trinity. Notice also in John 14:26: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send IN MY NAME(“Jesus”), he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I(Jesus) have said unto you” (KJV) - so if the Spirit comes in the name of Jesus, teaching the teachings of Jesus, and with the authority of Jesus, obviously it has the same name: “JESUS”- the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Notice also how Jesus HAD TO GO AWAY so that the “other” Comforter could come (Jn 16:7). This is why Paul could claim: “Now the Lord(Jesus) is that SPIRIT: and where the SPIRIT OF THE LORD is, there is liberty” (2 Cor 3:17 KJV); and why Jesus could say: “I am with you ALWAYS, even unto the end of the world. Amen” (Mt 28:20 KJV) - how could Jesus be with us ALWAYS if not as Spirit? “For I know that this shall turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the SPIRIT OF JESUS CHRIST” (Phil 1:19 KJV). Hence, “JESUS” is the singular NAME of the Son, of the Father, and of the Holy Spirit. Peter literally says IT IS THE ONLY NAME given to men for salvation (Acts 4:12). 


*** The Parallel passages of the Great Commission also show that the singular name of the Son, and of the Father, and of the Spirit is “JESUS”. The four accounts fit very naturally when you realize that Jesus gave the disciples commission-related instructions multiple times after his resurrection, both in Jerusalem and in Galilee, with the different Gospel writers emphasizing different occasions. The basic message was consistent in all four: Jesus sent his disciples to all nations, to preach the gospel, call people to repentance/faith, baptize believers, and proclaim the remission/forgiveness of sins, beginning from Jerusalem and extending to the whole world. The four accounts at a glance: (1) Matthew 28:16-20: It specifically lists the eleven disciples at Galilee(v.16), “some doubted” (v.17) - John clarifies that Thomas wasn’t present the first time Jesus appeared, and doubted (Lk 24:24-25); then Jesus sends them to all nations, to teach, and to baptize in the singular “name” of the Son, and of the Father, and of the Holy Ghost. (2) Mark 16:14-20: Mark specifically mentions that there were eleven, and that some had “hardness of heart” (probably referring to Thomas as well) because they “believed not them which had seen him after he was risen” (v.14) - this means that Jesus had already appeared to other people before. Paul gives an important summary: “And that he was seen of Cephas, then of the twelve: After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once..after that, he was seen of James; then of all the apostles” (1 Cor 15:5-7 KJV) - so Jesus obviously appeared multiple times to the apostles, involving different groups and occasions. Therefore, it is entirely reasonable for the Gospel writers to record different commissioning instructions given during different appearances, OR each writer explaining the Great Commission in their own words as they understood the core message. Mark then states that Jesus told them to go “into all the world” and “preach the gospel” (v.15), baptize them, and that many great things will be done “in my name” (Jesus, v.17). (3) Luke 24:45-49: Luke’s account of the Great Commission includes  the two Emmaus disciples (v.13), the eleven disciples, and “those with them”(v.33) However, “the Eleven” can function as the title/name of the apostolic body, not necessarily a headcount of eleven physically present. John 20:24 says Thomas was absent from the Easter-evening appearance. Luke’s account is most likely in Jerusalem, as the narrative mentions the two disciples from Emmaus as being in Jerusalem (v.18), and the Great Commission specifically says; “beginning from Jerusalem..” (v.47). Jesus “opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures” (v.45). John says “he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost” (Jn 20:22 KJV) - hence, Jesus opened their understanding by breathing the Holy Ghost onto them. Then Jesus delivers the Great Commission, as described by Luke: “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached IN HIS NAME among ALL NATIONS, beginning in Jerusalem” (v.47). Notice how they couldn’t go to all the nations (Gentiles) until they had been empowered to do so by the Holy Spirit(v.49), and that power arrived in Acts 2. So, in Luke, we see the same substance as Matthew and Mark: go to ALL NATIONS preaching, teaching, and baptizing. Luke does not use the word “baptize,” but he says: “repentance and remission of sins should be preached,” and since he also wrote the book of Acts, in Acts 2:38, after the promise of the Holy Spirit finally empowers them (Lk 24:49; Acts 2:4), he clarifies how you preach "repentance and remission of sins,” he said: “Repent, and BE BAPTIZED every one of you IN THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost” (KJV). (4) John 20: 21-23: John starts by saying that Jesus said: “Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send i you” (v.21) - John records the same words that Luke recorded: “Peace be unto you” (Lk 24:36), then says Jesus sends them as the Father sent him. We know from the parallel accounts that this “sending” is to ALL THE NATIONS of the world. Then John states that Jesus “breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost” (v.22) - from Luke's account we know that this means that “opened he their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures” (Lk 24:45 KJV). Finally, Jesus says: “Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained” (v.23) - this is a very controversial verse since Roman Catholicism uses it to claim that Jesus gave the apostles (and their successors) the power and authority to forgive sins. But in view of the parallel passages, Luke gives clarity to the meaning of this verse: “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name” (Lk 24:47 KJV) - hence, “to retain sin” is not withhold from sharing the gospel, and “to remit sin” is to preach the good news. After Jesus ascends into heaven, the disciples obey Jesus’ Great Commission, and Peter uses the “keys of heaven” for the first time in Acts 2:38: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost” (Acts 2:38 KJV) - notice the singular name, and notice its purpose: Jesus, for the forgiveness of sins. This is the key to heaven which Peter shared in Acts 2:38. 


*** The name invoked at baptism is “JESUS,” not a nameless vague Trinity. The Trinity describes the name of Jesus, not the other way around: “And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, CALLING ON THE NAME OF THE LORD” (Acts 22:16 KJV) - notice the name of “JESUS”(the name of the Lord) is explicitly invoked at baptism. That’s why James 2:7 says: “Is it not they who slander and blaspheme that precious name(singular name) by which you are distinguished and called [the name of Christ invoked in baptism]?” (James 2:7 AMPC) or “Is it not they who blaspheme the honorable name(singular name) which was INVOKED OVER YOU?” (James 2:7 RSV). THE NAME IS ALWAYS “JESUS”: “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the NAME(singular, only “Jesus” fulfills all three titles, you can see that in Isaiah 9:6) of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost” (Mt 28:19 KJV); “Go and make disciples of all the nations IN MY NAME(Jesus)” (Mt 28:19 as cited by Eusebius of Caesarea, Constantine’s historian, before the Council of Nicaea); “IN MY NAME(Jesus) shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues…” (Mk 16:17 KJV); “that repentance and remission of sins should be preached IN HIS NAME(Jesus) among all nations” (Lk 24:47 KJV); “Repent, and be baptized every one of you IN THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST for the remission of sins” (Acts 2:38 KJV); “But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and THE NAME OF JESUS CHRIST, they were baptized, both men and women” (Acts 8:12 KJV); “...only they were baptized IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS” (Acts 8:16 KJV);  “And he commanded them TO BE BAPTIZED IN THE NAME OF THE LORD(Jesus)” (Acts 10:48 KJV); “When they heard this, they were baptized IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS” (Acts 19:5 KJV) - Paul literally REBAPTIZED people so it could be done in Jesus’ name specifically(Acts 19:3-5); “Know ye not, that so many of us as were BAPTIZED INTO JESUS CHRIST were baptized into his death? Therefore we are BURIED with his BY BAPTISM into death…” (Rom 6:3-4 KJV) - notice how baptism is about Jesus’ death, not a vague, nameless Trinity, and notice how we are BURIED in water, not sprinkled like how the institutionalized religion does it; “Is Christ divided? was Paul crucified for you? or were ye baptized in the name of Paul?” (1 Cor 1:13 KJV) - no, they were not baptized in the name of Paul, they were baptized in the name of Jesus; “For as many of you as have been BAPTIZED INTO CHRIST have put on Christ” (Gal 3:27 KJV) - you are baptized into Christ, not into a Trinity; “Buried with HIM(Jesus) in baptism” (Col 2:12 KJV) - buried with HIM(Jesus), not a Trinity. 


*** Col 2:9-10 says the fullness of the Godhead is in Jesus, and that we are COMPLETE in Him. Jesus declares the Father's name (Jn 17:26). Jesus manifested the Father's name (Jn 17:6). Who receives Jesus receives the Father (Jn 13:20). Who believes in Jesus believes in the Father (Jn 12:44). If you know Jesus you know the Father (Jn 8:19). Honoring the Son you honor the Father (Jn 5:23). We gather in the name of Jesus (Mt 18:20). Whatever we ask we ask in the name of Jesus (Jn 16:23). We pray and make requests in Jesus' name (Jn 14:13-14). We do signs and wonders in Jesus' name (Acts 4:30). We pray for the sick in Jesus’ name (Jms 5:14). We cast out devils and speak in tongues in Jesus’ name (Mk 16:17-18). We teach & preach in Jesus' name (Acts 4:17-18). Every knee should bow to Jesus (Phil 2:9-10). There is no salvation in any other name other than Jesus (Acts 4:12). You will be hated for Jesus' name (Acts 4:10). You will risk your life for Jesus' name (Acts 15:26). Persecuted for Jesus’ name (Acts 5:28). Jesus means YHWH-savior. All the Apostles baptized in Jesus' name. Yet, why do most Christians follow the Traditions of men rather that God’s Word by baptizing in a vague, nameless Trinity? “And whatsoever ye do in word or deed(baptism is a deed), DO ALL IN THE NAME OF THE LORD JESUS, giving thanks to God and the Father by him” (Col 3:17 KJV).


Matthew 28:20: “..lo, I am with you always…”: Only omnipresent God can be everywhere present with all believers at all times until the end of the age. In Jn 14:17-18, Jesus promised: “I will not leave you comfortless(or “as orphans,” BSB, aka “without a FATHER”): I[Jesus] will come to you(as a HOLY SPIRIT),” or how can Jesus be with us always if not AS SPIRIT? That’s why Paul proclaimed: “the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty” (2 Cor 3:17 KJV).
